title: computeSpmConcentrations reaches through state.raw() and re-derives the arena addressing that BasicBatchView::at already computes

verdict.reason:
Both quotes are verbatim. SpmObservables.hpp:300-303 is exactly `const auto *first_mode = state.raw().data() + static_cast<std::size_t>(layout.z[d].row_begin) * state.stride() + static_cast<std::size_t>(c);`, and BatchView.hpp:76-83 is exactly the `at(StateSlice, int, int)` shown, returning `values_[(slice.row_begin + row) * shape_.stride + lane]`. Substituting row=0 collapses to `values_[row_begin*stride + lane]` -- byte-identical address, so the loads inside `concentrationOutput` are the same values.

DIGIT-IDENTICAL: yes. The proposal touches only the base-pointer computation; it does not enter `spm_scalar::concentrationOutput` (SpmScalarKernels.hpp:239-252), whose accumulation loop `for (mode...) result += coefficients[mode] * first_mode[mode * mode_stride];` is untouched. No reassociation, no fusion, no loop replacement.

TYPES: `state` is `const BasicBatchView<const Real> &` (SpmObservables.hpp:248), so `at()` returns `const Real&` and `&state.at(...)` is `const Real*` -- the same type as `state.raw().data()`, deducing `State = Real` against the callee's `const State *first_mode`. Compiles unchanged.

NOT A FALSE "DUPLICATE": the proposed form is already the established idiom in this very file. computeSpmSurfaceConcentrations at line 229 writes `state.at(layout.z[d], mode, lane)` over the same slice, and lines 288/290/293 use `state.at(layout.<slice>[d], 0, c)`. Line 300 is the sole outlier -- and `grep raw\(\)` over SpmObservables.hpp returns exactly one hit (line 300), so the reviewer's claim (b) that this is the only `raw()` escape hatch in the kernel is confirmed for the whole file.

CONTRACTS (PLAN.md:155-186): none violated. PC-1 (no hot-path allocation) -- `at()` is an inline non-allocating member. PC-2/PC-5 -- non-virtual, concrete type, no std::function. PC-10 (one physics source) -- this removes duplicated *addressing*, not physics; the formula stays single-sourced in SpmScalarKernels.hpp. MC-5 -- SpmObservables.hpp is `@surface internal` (line 22) and BatchView.hpp is `@surface support` (line 9); internal including support is the allowed direction, and BatchView.hpp is already included at line 27, so the change adds no dependency.

TWO OVERSTATEMENTS IN THE RATIONALE (they qualify, not refute): (i) claim (c) is only half-true -- line 308 still hands `state.stride()` to the callee as `mode_stride`, so the row_begin/stride coupling is encapsulated for the base address but the stride remains hand-passed; (ii) claim (a)'s assert is partial -- `at(..., 0, c)` validates only mode 0, while the kernel then walks `first_mode[mode * mode_stride]` for mode in [0, NCH). The existing assert at lines 256-257 (`layout.z[d].rows == NCH`) plus `at()`'s `slice.row_begin + row < shape_.n_rows` still leaves the top mode unchecked. Strictly better than the zero bounds-checking of the current line, but not full coverage.

Gates exist to confirm: tests/unit/core_SpmObservables_test.cpp:97,126,132,186 and tests/unit/core_ChebyshevTransient_test.cpp:168 both call computeSpmConcentrations directly, so the change is verifiable by execution rather than inspection, as the reviewer asks.

title: SpmObservableScratch sizes its storage from a bare literal 21 that must be hand-counted against view()'s 21 take() calls, and the only guard runs after the subspans have already been formed
The surface-stoichiometry validity gate is a bare floating-point range test in a translation unit compiled with -Ofast -ffast-math, exactly the construct Numeric.hpp documents as unreliable there

verdict.reason:
CODE EXISTS VERBATIM. SpmObservables.hpp:463-468 is exactly as quoted: `const Real cs = output.concentration[d][lane]; const Real z_surface = spm_scalar::surfaceStoichiometry(cs, electrode.cs_max); if (!(primal_value(z_surface) > 0.0 && primal_value(z_surface) < 1.0)) return slide::Status::Invalid_states;`. Numeric.hpp:24-37 is quoted correctly, including "`std::isfinite` is not a validation primitive in those builds because the compiler is permitted to assume NaN and infinity never occur and fold the check to true" and the volatile/bit_cast remedy. Grep for `is_finite_primal|is_finite` across SpmObservables.hpp returns ZERO hits -- line 467 is the only Invalid_states return in the whole header, so no upstream finite guard rescues it.

BUILD IS REALLY FAST-MATH. StandardProjectSettings.cmake:58-59 (Clang) and 64-65 (GCC) add `-Ofast` and `-ffast-math` under `$<$<AND:$<CONFIG:Release>,$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CXX>>`. SlideCoreTarget.cmake:49-51 restores strict FP for exactly two files, as claimed.

BUT THE NAMED TU IS WRONG -- and this nearly killed the finding. SpmBatch.cpp's own header comment says: "This file deliberately does NOT include `SpmPipeline.hpp` -- the batch reaches its implementation only through the type-erased pointers the factory installs, which is what makes the erasure real." The reviewer's stated chain is false. The finding survives via a different TU: SpmFactory.cpp:9 `#include "SpmPipeline.hpp"` -> SpmPipeline.hpp:11 `#include "SpmDiffusionRhs.hpp"` -> SpmDiffusionRhs.hpp:17 `#include "SpmObservables.hpp"`. SpmFactory.cpp is at SlideCoreTarget.cmake:45 and is NOT in the strict-fp list. So the kernel IS instantiated under -Ofast. Conclusion holds, premise does not.

TWO SIBLINGS CONFIRM THE ASYMMETRY IS A DEFECT, NOT A STYLE CHOICE. The reviewer cites SpmStress.hpp:162-163 (`if (!is_finite_primal(maximum)) return slide::Status::Numerical_failure;`) correctly. Stronger and uncited: the CUDA twin of this exact gate, CudaSpmRuntime.cu:119-121, writes `if (!(surface_stoichiometry[domain] > 0.0 && surface_stoichiometry[domain] < 1.0) || !isfinite(surface_stoichiometry[domain]))` -- the same range test PLUS the finite disjunct the proposal asks for. The GPU path guards; the CPU path does not. Separately ForwardSensitivity.cpp:97 carries the identical bare range test and is one of the two files placed under strict FP -- consistent with the hazard being known and handled everywhere except here.

INCLUDE CLAIM IS WRONG BUT HARMLESS. "transitively via CellDesign/StateArena" is backwards: CellDesign.hpp:9 -> StateArena.hpp, which includes no project headers; Numeric.hpp:9 includes StateArena, not the reverse. The real route is SpmObservables.hpp:29 `#include "CompiledCurve.hpp"` -> CompiledCurve.hpp:10 `#include "Numeric.hpp"`. So it compiles, but only by accident of a third party's include.

TEST-GAP IS PARTIAL, NOT TOTAL. tests/unit/core_SpmElectrical_test.cpp:160-186 already covers assertion one: arena built with `// zero z => invalid zero surface concentration` and REQUIRE(... == Status::Invalid_states) at :184-185. That test passes under -Ofast regardless, because cs is exactly 0 so `0.0 > 0.0` is an ordinary finite comparison. Only the cs>=cs_max and NaN assertions are new; the NaN one is the load-bearing one.

NaN MECHANISM MISDESCRIBED. SpmScalarKernels.hpp: `concentrationOutput` returns `modal_sum + feedthrough * flux / diffusivity`. With diffusivity=0 and flux!=0 you get inf, not NaN; NaN requires 0/0, i.e. diffusivity=0 AND flux=0 -- which the existing harness already gives via `const std::array<double,1> iapp{};` (:179). Not "inf-inf" as written. NaN is reachable, but by the other route.

UNVERIFIED CLAIM: "The third assertion is the one that fails today under -Ofast" is a prediction, not a measured result -- I did not build Release and observe the fold, and whether clang actually elides the compare is version/pipeline dependent. Per the repo's own register-before-run standard this must be stated as [inferred]. The finding stands as a latent-defect/hardening item on the strength of the repo's own documented hazard plus two correct siblings, not on a demonstrated miscompile.

DIGIT-IDENTICAL: yes. The added term is a short-circuited boolean with no FP arithmetic, no reassociation, no FMA fusion, no summation reordering. Under strict IEEE the accept/reject set is unchanged: finite z in (0,1) -> is_finite_primal true, `!true` false, short-circuits to the existing test; NaN -> already rejected; Inf -> `inf < 1.0` already false, already rejected. Only the compiler's licence to delete the rejection is removed.

CONTRACTS (PLAN.md 1.1-1.3, read at :147-186): PC-1 zero heap allocations per step -- guard allocates nothing. PC-2/no per-cell virtual dispatch and no std::function -- none added. PC-3 SoA -- untouched. PC-10 "ONE physics source: every formula exists in exactly one scalar-generic definition" (:164) -- the proposal CALLS the shared Numeric.hpp helper instead of open-coding a bit-cast classifier, so it serves PC-10 rather than violating it. MC-5/D-42 "no api or support header may include an internal one" (:1243) -- direction here is internal -> support: SpmObservables.hpp:22 is `@surface internal`, Numeric.hpp:4 is `@surface support`. That direction is permitted; the forbidden one is the reverse. No violation.
verdict.revised_proposal:
Apply the guard as proposed at SpmObservables.hpp:466, but fix the include, the TU attribution, and the test recipe.

1) Code change (unchanged from the proposal, it is correct):

      if (!is_finite_primal(z_surface)
          || !(primal_value(z_surface) > 0.0 && primal_value(z_surface) < 1.0))
        return slide::Status::Invalid_states;

2) Add an EXPLICIT `#include "Numeric.hpp"` to the include block at SpmObservables.hpp:27-31. Do not rely on the transitive path through CompiledCurve.hpp:10 -- the reviewer's stated route (CellDesign/StateArena) does not exist, and the real route is an IWYU accident that a future include-pruning pass would silently break, restoring the bug with no diff at the call site.

3) Correct the commit/PR wording: the fast-math TU that instantiates this kernel is src/core/SpmFactory.cpp (SpmFactory.cpp:9 -> SpmPipeline.hpp:11 -> SpmDiffusionRhs.hpp:17 -> SpmObservables.hpp), NOT SpmBatch.cpp, which its own header comment documents as deliberately excluding SpmPipeline.hpp.

4) Registered test in tests/unit/core_SpmObservables_test.cpp, with the band stated before running:
   - cs <= 0 -> Invalid_states. NOTE: already covered by tests/unit/core_SpmElectrical_test.cpp:160-186; either extend that test or cross-reference it rather than duplicating the harness (MC-4).
   - cs >= cs_max -> Invalid_states. New; passes today under both configs.
   - NaN lane -> Invalid_states. New and load-bearing. Build it as diffusion_coefficient row = 0.0 WITH i_app = 0 so `feedthrough * flux / diffusivity` evaluates 0/0; the reviewer's "inf-inf" description is wrong and a nonzero i_app yields inf (already rejected by `inf < 1.0`), which would silently not exercise the hazard.
   - Add a fourth lane with z = +inf to cover the `ninf` half of -ffinite-math-only, which the proposal's guard also closes but the registered band did not mention.
   Assert in BOTH Debug and Release; the Release run is the only one that can fail.

5) Downgrade the claim "the third assertion fails today under -Ofast" to [inferred] until a Release build is actually run and the verdict recorded. If the third assertion PASSES in Release, the finding does not die -- it becomes hardening that keeps the CPU gate in line with CudaSpmRuntime.cu:119-121 and SpmStress.hpp:162-163 -- but the report must say so rather than assert a miscompile that was never observed.

title: computeSpmObservables takes a 23-span, 368-byte struct by value on the per-step hot path
evidence:
SpmObservables.hpp:434-441:
  template <int NCH, class Real>
  [[nodiscard]] slide::Status computeSpmObservables(const SpmElectricalParams<NCH> &p,
                                                    const BasicBatchView<const Real> &state,
                                                    const SpmStateLayout &layout,
                                                    const BasicStepCtx<Real> &ctx,
                                                    BasicSpmObservables<Real>
                                                      output,
                                                    SpmTransportCache *cache = nullptr)

BasicSpmObservables (SpmObservables.hpp:340-359) holds 7 PerDomain<std::span<Real>> (= 14 spans) plus 9 bare spans = 23 spans = 368 bytes on a 64-bit target. Every parameter before it is correctly a reference; only this one is by value.

The sibling kernel gets it right -- src/core/SpmStress.hpp:89-93 takes the big one by const reference and only the 3-span output by value:
  [[nodiscard]] slide::Status computeSpmStress(const SpmStressParams<NCH> &p,
                                               const BasicSpmObservables<Real> &observables,
                                               int n_lanes,
                                               BasicSpmStress<Real>
                                                 output)
proposal:
Change the parameter to `const BasicSpmObservables<Real> &output`. std::span's constness does not propagate to the pointee, so every `output.terminal_voltage[lane] = ...` write inside the body still compiles unchanged and writes to the same caller-owned storage. Purely a copy elimination -- digit-identical, and it matches the convention SpmStress.hpp already follows.

While in the signature: add `noexcept` to the trivially non-throwing accessors in this subsystem that lack it and where it is free and correct -- SpmObservables.hpp:73 `int lanes() const`, :76 `std::size_t index(...) const`, :408 `int n_lanes() const`, SpectralDiffusion.hpp:158-159 `const DiffusionParams<NCH> &params() const` / `int n_lanes() const`, and Dual.hpp:64-103 (exp/expm1/sqrt/pow/asinh/abs are all noexcept in fact). Mark the value-returning ones [[nodiscard]].

verdict.reason:
VERIFIED AT SOURCE. src/core/SpmObservables.hpp:434-441 is quoted verbatim — `BasicSpmObservables<Real>\n    output,` is the only non-reference parameter; p/state/layout/ctx are all `const ... &`. The struct at :340-359 counts exactly as claimed: 7 `PerDomain<std::span<Real>>` (concentration, effective_diffusivity, molar_flux, surface_stoichiometry, exchange_current_density, overpotential, electrode_ocv) + 9 bare spans (entropic_coefficient, negative_entropic_coefficient, open_circuit_voltage, resistance, terminal_voltage, reversible_heat, reaction_heat, ohmic_heat, total_heat). `PerDomain` is `using PerDomain = std::array<T, 2>;` (src/core/CellDesign.hpp:42), so 7*2+9 = 23 spans; a dynamic-extent span is ptr+size = 16 B on a 64-bit target, so 368 B. Arithmetic confirmed.

HOT PATH CONFIRMED: SpmPipeline.hpp:115 sits inside `[[nodiscard]] slide::Status evaluate(RhsViews &views, const StepCtx &ctx)` (SpmPipeline.hpp:107) — the per-stage RHS. Three more call sites at SpmPipeline.hpp:341, :479, :525.

DIGIT-IDENTICAL — I checked the two things that could break it, not just the span-constness argument:
(1) The body (lines 443-545) never rebinds a member of `output`; every use is either a read `output.concentration[d][lane]` (:463, :496, :500-501, :525, :535-536) or a write through the span `output.X[...] = ...`. On a const object `std::array::operator[]` yields `const std::span<Real>&`, whose `operator[]` yields `Real&` — writes compile and land in the same caller-owned storage.
(2) The forwarding call at :449-451 passes `output.concentration/.effective_diffusivity/.molar_flux` into `computeSpmSurfaceConcentrations`, whose params (SpmObservables.hpp:208-213) are `PerDomain<std::span<Real>>` BY VALUE — copy-initialising a std::array from a const lvalue is well-formed, so const& on `output` does not break the forward.
(3) Call-site binding: SpmPipeline passes lvalues (:112 `observable_view`, :523 `observable`); tests/unit/core_SpmElectrical_test.cpp:184 passes the prvalue `scratch.view()`, which binds to const& with lifetime through the full-expression, and its spans point into `scratch`, which outlives the call. No arithmetic touched anywhere — no reassociation, no FMA fusion, no loop restructuring.

NO CONTRACT VIOLATION. PLAN.md:153-166: PC-1 is "ZERO heap allocations per accepted step" — a by-value struct copy is stack/register, so removing it neither creates nor cures a PC-1 issue. PC-2/PC-5 (no virtual dispatch, no std::function) untouched. PC-10 (one physics source) untouched — no formula moves. The noexcept half actively supports PC-4 ("No exceptions ... on the hot path", PLAN.md:158). MC-5 unaffected (no surface added).

TWO DEFECTS IN THE REVIEWER'S REASONING, neither fatal to the finding:
(a) The "sibling gets it right" rationale MISREADS the house convention. SpmStress.hpp:89-93 takes its own OUTPUT bundle `BasicSpmStress<Real>\n  output` BY VALUE too — it takes `observables` by const& because there it is an INPUT. The actual convention is "inputs by const&, output span-bundles by value", and under that reading computeSpmObservables is currently CONFORMING, not deviant. The finding stands on the 368-byte size alone, not on consistency.
(b) Line slip: `int lanes() const` is at SpmObservables.hpp:74, not :73 (`index(...)` at :76 is correct).

NOEXCEPT/NODISCARD RIDER CHECKED AND SAFE: Dual.hpp:64-103 confirmed — exp/expm1/sqrt/pow/asinh/abs call only std::exp/expm1/sqrt/pow/asinh and Dual's constexpr operator-, none of which throw. SpectralDiffusion.hpp:158-159 confirmed verbatim (`const DiffusionParams<NCH> &params() const` / `int n_lanes() const`). I grepped src+tests for discarded calls to these accessors and found none, and there is no `-Werror`/`/WX` in CMakeLists.txt, so [[nodiscard]] cannot break the build.
verdict.revised_proposal:
Apply the core change: `const BasicSpmObservables<Real> &output` at SpmObservables.hpp:439-440. Digit-identical; no call site or forwarding call needs editing (verified above).

Correct the stated rationale before it lands: do NOT justify it as "matching SpmStress.hpp" — SpmStress passes its own output bundle by value (SpmStress.hpp:92-93), so the real justification is size alone (368 B vs 48 B for BasicSpmStress). To keep the convention coherent, add a one-line comment at the parameter, e.g. `//!< in-out span bundle; by const& because it is 23 spans (368 B) — spans stay mutable through const`, so the next reader does not "fix" it back to by-value for symmetry. Leave BasicSpmStress by value (3 spans = 48 B, cheaper than an indirection).

Noexcept rider: correct the cited line for `lanes()` to SpmObservables.hpp:74 (not :73). Then add `noexcept` to SpmObservables.hpp:74 `lanes()`, :76 `index(...)`, :408 `n_lanes()`, SpectralDiffusion.hpp:158-159 `params()`/`n_lanes()`, and Dual.hpp:64,70,75,82,94,100. Add [[nodiscard]] to the same value-returning accessors — verified free (no discarded call sites, no -Werror).

Recommended gate, since these are two independent changes: land the signature change alone first and prove it with a recorded digit-for-digit comparison of an SpmPipeline run before/after (a "no-op refactor" claim needs identical outputs on a recorded case, not code inspection); land the noexcept/[[nodiscard]] sweep as a separate commit that only needs a clean build.

title: SpmTransportCache publishes all seven buffers as public trailing-underscore members and names its accessor lanes(), against the M0.9 lexicon n_lanes() that every neighbouring class obeys

verdict.reason: Code exists verbatim. SpmObservables.hpp:68 opens `struct SpmTransportCache`; :74 `int lanes() const { return lanes_; }`; :82-89 declare `lanes_` and all seven buffers (`valid_`, `temperature_`, `diffusion_reference_`, `specific_area_`, `thickness_`, `effective_diffusivity_`, `flux_denominator_`); `private:` is :91 and covers only CheckedShape/the delegating ctor/checked_shape. So the representation is public while the ctor helper is hidden -- as claimed. The consumer at :136 is verbatim `assert(cache->lanes() == state.n_lanes());`. TWO REVIEWER ERRORS. (1) "every neighbouring class obeys" is FALSE: src/core/PackSolver.hpp:39 reads `int lanes() const { return lanes_; }` and PackSolver.hpp:4 is `@surface api`, i.e. the other offender is on the PUBLIC surface. Twelve peers do use n_lanes() (StateArena:185, BatchView:87 -- reviewer cited 85, AgeingKernel:63, SpectralDiffusion:159, SpmObservables:408, Recorder:81/141, AsyncRecorder:254, SpmFactory:100, SpmPipeline:612, CudaSpmBatch.hpp:58). (2) The MC-5 justification misreads the contract: SpmObservables.hpp:22 is `@surface internal`, and PLAN.md:186 + D-42 (PLAN.md:1243) operationalize MC-5 as header-tier classification ("no api or support header may include an internal one"), enforced by R1-R6 in tests/structural/p9c5_public_surface.cmake, whose R4 pins api headers only -- this file is not pinned. MC-5 is already satisfied here by tier; the change is hygiene, not contract repair. GATE SAFETY: R6's P9C5_FORBIDDEN_TOKENS (p9c5_public_surface.cmake:289-297) lists nLanes(/nRows(/checkedLaneCount/... but NOT `lanes(`, so today's spelling trips nothing; and it cannot be added naively because :317 matches via `string(FIND)` on compacted text, so the token "lanes(" would fire on every legitimate `n_lanes(`. pc10_single_source.cmake:72 does load this file and require_tokens spm_scalar::arrheniusFactor(/activatedValue(/fluxDenominator(/molarFlux( -- the proposal leaves all arithmetic in the kernel, so PC-10 holds. DIGIT-IDENTITY: the sole consumer of the public buffers repo-wide is computeSpmTransportLane itself (:136-163); SpmPipeline.hpp:98-99,120,130,304-305,440,484,524,734,736 only constructs caches and passes addresses, and tests/unit/core_AgeingKernel_test.cpp:575-577 touches only the throwing ctors. Returning flux_denominator from try_load lets the kernel call spm_scalar::molarFlux on bit-identical operands; the miss path keeps the four spm_scalar:: calls in the same order. No reassociation/fusion/allocation; only `index()` is recomputed once on a miss (integer). Hardcoding real_t in the signatures is safe: the branch is guarded by `if constexpr (std::is_same_v<std::remove_cv_t<Real>, real_t>)` and Real is necessarily non-const since :169 assigns through `Real &`.
verdict.revised_proposal: Apply the mechanical extraction as proposed -- rename lanes()->n_lanes(), lanes_->n_lanes_, move the seven buffers plus n_lanes_ and index() behind `private:`, and expose exactly try_load(...)/store(...) as the two operations the kernel performs -- but with three amendments. (1) Drop the MC-5 justification and state the real one: SpmObservables.hpp:22 is `@surface internal`, so MC-5 (PLAN.md:186, D-42 at PLAN.md:1243) is already satisfied by header tier; this is class-level encapsulation hygiene plus removal of the exact-equality key comparison from the kernel body, which is worth doing on its own merits. (2) Keep ALL arithmetic in the kernel -- try_load returns effective_diffusivity and flux_denominator, store accepts them; do NOT move the spm_scalar:: calls into store(), or the physics migrates into the cache and the intent of pc10_single_source.cmake:72's require_tokens is hollowed out even though the substring gate would still pass. (3) Fix PackSolver.hpp:39 in the same pass -- it is the same `lanes()` spelling in an `@surface api` header, so leaving it converts a two-site inconsistency into a one-site one on the more visible surface. If the lexicon is to be made inductive rather than merely tidied, add to R6 a FORBIDDEN_REGEX entry anchored on a non-identifier predecessor, e.g. "[^_a-zA-Z0-9]lanes\\(", since :317's string(FIND) substring match makes the bare token "lanes(" unusable (it matches inside every n_lanes().

title: computeSpmStress writes the half-sphere-to-full-sphere mirror index algebra twice, rebuilds a loop-invariant coordinate array on every call, and contains one write that is never read
proposal:
Two small helpers, both of which make the code read as the algorithm.

(a) Name the node-major access once, next to the comment that documents it (SpmObservables.hpp):
  template <class Real>
  [[nodiscard]] constexpr std::span<Real> node_row(std::span<Real> profile, int node, int n_lanes) noexcept
  { return profile.subspan(static_cast<std::size_t>(node) * n_lanes, static_cast<std::size_t>(n_lanes)); }
All seven sites become `node_row(obs.concentration[d], node, L)[lane]`, which also makes the per-node span available to std::ranges algorithms for a future lane sweep.

(b) Name the mirror once (SpmStress.hpp, file-local detail::):
  template <class T, class U, std::size_t Half, class Transform>
  constexpr void mirrorToFullSphere(const std::array<T, Half> &half,
                                    std::array<U, 2 * Half - 1> &full,
                                    Transform left_transform);
  // full[i] = left_transform(half[i]) for i in [0, Half-2]
  // full[Half-1] = half[Half-1]                       (centre)
  // full[Half+i] = half[Half-2-i] for i in [0, Half-2] (right, reversed)
called with `std::negate<>{}` for the coordinates and `std::identity{}` for the concentrations. Delete the dead `positive_x[NCH + 1] = 0.0;`.

(c) Separately: positive_x/full_x are functions of p.x_inner alone and are rebuilt on every computeSpmStress call, i.e. once per RHS evaluation. Precompute them in SpmStressParams (a `std::array<real_t, full_nodes> node_coordinate{}` filled by a cold builder next to validateSpmStressParams) so the hot function only reads them. This is pure hoisting of an identical computation -- the values are bit-identical -- but it does change what validateSpmStressParams must check, so land it with the recorded-bits gate as the arbiter.

NOT proposed: hoisting `concentration[column] * full_x[column] * full_x[column]` out of the row loop at SpmStress.hpp:130-135. It would save (2*NCH+3)^2 -> (2*NCH+3) multiplications per lane per domain, but it reassociates ((Q*c)*x)*x into Q*((c*x)*x), which is NOT digit-identical and would break the recorded-bit contract. Flagging it here so the next reviewer does not propose it without that caveat.

verdict.reason: Code exists verbatim. SpmStress.hpp:112-117 `full_x[centre] = 0.0; for (int i = 0; i < NCH + 1; ++i) { full_x[i] = -positive_x[i]; full_x[NCH + 2 + i] = positive_x[NCH - i]; }` and SpmStress.hpp:123-127 `concentration[centre] = observables.concentration[d][(NCH+1)*L + lane]; for (int i = 0; i < NCH + 1; ++i) { concentration[i] = observables.concentration[d][i*L + lane]; concentration[NCH+2+i] = observables.concentration[d][(NCH-i)*L + lane]; }` are the same index map element-for-element (left i in [0,NCH], centre at NCH+1, right NCH+2+i <- NCH-i), and both sources run surface->centre (positive_x[0]=1.0 surface, positive_x[NCH+1]=0.0 centre; concentration node 0 = surface, node NCH+1 = centre per SpmObservables.hpp:305-317), so it is not a numerically meaningful "duplicate". DEAD WRITE CONFIRMED: positive_x is read only at line 115 (`positive_x[i]`, i in [0,NCH]) and line 116 (`positive_x[NCH - i]`, i in [0,NCH] -> indices [0,NCH]); index NCH+1 is never loaded, and `std::array<real_t, half_nodes> positive_x{}` (line 107) already zeroed it. NOT ALREADY DONE: `grep -rni "mirror|full_sphere|fullSphere" src/` returns only unrelated comments (CudaSpmBatch.hpp:20 "Owns one CPU metadata/state mirror", SpectralDiffusionLegacy.hpp:25 "mirrors legacy exactly") -- no such helper exists. Idiom count verified: SpmObservables.hpp:305,316,317 and SpmStress.hpp:123,125,126,154 = seven in the two named files, but the reviewer UNDERCOUNTS the reach -- SurfaceCrack.hpp:104 `observables.concentration[neg][static_cast<std::size_t>(layout.z[neg].rows + 1) * L + i]` is an eighth site in a third file (and :103 `observables.concentration[neg][i]` is an implicit node-0 ninth). THREE FLAWS IN THE PROPOSAL. This exercises the quadrature at a genuinely non-uniform operating point, which the uniform case does not.

title: Five of the ten headers in this subsystem carry a two-line brief instead of the MC-3 contract comment the other five demonstrate
evidence:

 * @file SpmDiffusionRhs.hpp
 * @brief The solid-diffusion modal RHS mapping.

 * @file SpmStress.hpp

- Numeric.hpp: state the invariant that makes the file exist -- these are the ONLY validation predicates safe under the -Ofast/-ffast-math Release build (cmake/StandardProjectSettings.cmake:58-59); std::isfinite and bare comparisons are not. verdict.reason:

Nothing arrhenius-related. So no test covers this duplication, AND, importantly, the proposed edit turns no existing gate red.

DIGIT-IDENTICAL: YES -- but the reviewer's stated justification is WRONG, and the correct reason is stronger. The reviewer writes "for Real=Dual a double lifted to Dual has zero derivative so Dual/Dual reduces to the same primal quotient and the same a'/b tangent as the current Dual/double form." There is no current Dual/double form. Dual.hpp:58 declares exactly one division operator, `constexpr Dual operator/(Dual left, Dual right) { return left /= right; }`, and Dual.hpp:21 `constexpr Dual(real_t primal) : value{ primal } {}` is a non-explicit converting constructor. SeiParams.hpp:35,39 / LamParams.hpp:35,37 / LithiumPlatingParams.hpp:23,27 all declare `real_t Rg{ 8.314 }` and `real_t reference_temperature{ 298.15 }`, i.e. plain double. So `Real{1} / p.reference_temperature` with Real=Dual ALREADY implicitly lifts the double to `Dual{x, 0.0}` and calls operator/(Dual,Dual). The proposed `static_cast<Real>(...)` produces that same `Dual{x, 0.0}` -- a semantic no-op. This matters, because Dual::operator/= at :46-52 computes `derivative = (derivative * other.value - value * other.derivative) / (other.value * other.value)`, which for db=0 is `d*b/(b*b)`, NOT `d/b`. Had the reviewer's premise held (a real Dual/double overload returning `d/b`), the change would NOT have been digit-identical. The conclusion survives only because both sides are already Dual/Dual. Operation order is otherwise identical: kernel is `(Scalar{1.0}/reference_temperature - Scalar{1.0}/temperature) / gas_constant`, matching the call sites token for token; `Real{1}` and `Scalar{1.0}` are the same value (int 1 is a constant expression exactly representable as double, so the braced init is not narrowing). No reassociation, no FMA fusion, no summation-order change.

NO CONTRACT VIOLATION. MC-5 per PLAN.md:1243 (D-42) is "no api or support header may include an internal one" -- the forbidden direction is the reverse of this change. SpmScalarKernels.hpp:10 is `@surface support`; Sei.hpp:4, Lam.hpp:4, LithiumPlating.hpp:4, SurfaceCrack.hpp:4 are all `@surface internal`. Internal including support is permitted. PLAN.md:1243 also records precedent that "PC-10 (one physics source) outranks MC-5" where they collide. arrheniusFactor is header-inline, SLIDE_SPM_HOST_DEVICE, noexcept: no hot-path allocation, no per-cell virtual dispatch, no std::function. The change satisfies PC-10 (PLAN.md:164 "ONE physics source: every formula exists in exactly one scalar-generic definition") rather than violating anything.

SURFACECRACK EXCLUSION IS CORRECTLY REASONED. Converting :126-127 would give `exp(k_activation * ((1/Tref - 1/T)/Rg))` versus the current `exp((k_activation/Rg) * (1/Tref - 1/T))`. (k/Rg)*x and k*(x/Rg) are two different rounding sequences. Leaving it out is right, and the proposed forbid token would not accidentally fire on it either: crack compacts to `.../T));` and the token demands `/T)/p.Rg`.
verdict.revised_proposal:
Apply the proposal as written for the three identical sites, with three corrections/refinements.

The true reason is: Dual.hpp declares only operator/(Dual,Dual) (:58) and a non-explicit Dual(real_t) ctor (:21), so with real_t params the call sites already perform Dual/Dual against a zero-derivative divisor; static_cast<Real>(...) is a semantic no-op yielding the identical Dual{x, 0.0}. Both before and after evaluate Dual::operator/= as (d*b - v*0)/(b*b) (:48-49). The overstated version would be a false digit-identity claim, since operator/= does not compute d/b.

(2) Edit at Sei.hpp:73, Lam.hpp:84, LithiumPlating.hpp:71:
  const Real arrhenius = spm_scalar::arrheniusFactor(
    static_cast<Real>(p.reference_temperature), T, static_cast<Real>(p.Rg));
matching the existing idiom at SpmObservables.hpp:457-458 verbatim.                                            const Real &driving_potential)

title: The cell constitutive relation I = (E - (V+ - V-))/R with its finiteness gauntlet is written out four times across three kernels

verdict.reason:
REAL. I opened all four sites and every quoted line matches byte-for-byte. `src/core/PackSolver.cpp:540-545` and `src/core/PackSolverIterative.cpp:169-174` are literally the same five statements (`voltage = candidate_node_voltage_[branch.node_positive] - candidate_node_voltage_[branch.node_negative];` / `numerator = ocv_[branch.cell] - voltage;` / finite gate / `candidate_current_[branch.cell] = numerator / resistance_[branch.cell];`). `PackSolver.cpp:578-582` is the same with inverted check polarity. `PackSolverIterative.cpp:64-67` is the same relation with `layer_voltage_[layer]` as the drop — same physics (I = (E - V_layer)/R), only the source of the drop differs, so a single `drop` parameter covers all four with NO flag or branch. Scoping is correct: `grep` for the formula returns exactly six hits, and the two the reviewer excluded (`PackSolver.cpp:443`, `PackSolverIterative.cpp:197`, both `voltage - ocv_[branch.cell]`) are the opposite-sign residual terms feeding a Kahan accumulation — genuinely a different computation, and `PackSolverIterative.cpp:198-199` says so ("The opposite subtraction was validated above when reconstructing this cell current"). No existing helper covers this: `PackSolverInternal.hpp` holds only `knownSolveMode`, `addFinite`, `addCompensatedFinite`, `finiteCandidate`, and `grep` for `branchDrop|cellCurrentFromDrop` across `src/` returns nothing — the reviewer's call-site sketch invents `branchDrop`, which does not exist and must be inlined or added.

DIGIT-IDENTICAL: yes, the arithmetic is preserved op-for-op — one subtraction then one division, no summation reordered, no loop replaced by `std::reduce`, no multiply-add fused. Two check-order shifts are equivalent, not merely similar: at site 1 the helper returns early on non-finite current before `difference` is computed, but `PackSolver.cpp:548` (`if (!is_finite(candidate_current_[branch.cell]) || !is_finite(difference))`) returns `Invalid_states` on that same condition, so no case diverges; the `difference` finiteness check must simply stay at the call site.

The reviewer's one stated "behavioural nuance" is a MISREADING and should be struck. He claims `PackSolver.cpp:582` writes `candidate_current_` on a failing path "whereas the helper leaves the old value". It does not diverge: his own helper body writes (`current = numerator / resistance; return is_finite(current);`) before returning false, so the non-finite-quotient case writes in both versions; and the non-finite-drop case writes in neither. The escape hatch he leans on is real (`PackSolver.cpp:340-343`: `if (status != slide::Status::Success) { workspace_.invalidate(); return status; }`), but it is not needed. Note also that the stale-read he worries about is already unreachable: `PackSolver.cpp:583` short-circuits on `!is_finite(voltage) || !is_finite(numerator)` before evaluating `is_finite(candidate_current_[...])`.

CONTRACTS: none violated. `PLAN.md:164` PC-10 ("ONE physics source: every formula exists in exactly one scalar-generic definition") is the rule the proposal serves; a `real_t`-concrete helper matches its `addFinite`/`addCompensatedFinite` siblings in the same header, and the pack solver is `real_t`-only throughout (`StateArena.hpp:34: using real_t = double`). PC-1/PC-2/PC-5 untouched — an inline free function, no allocation, no virtual dispatch, no `std::function`. PC-8 order unchanged. MC-5 satisfied: `PackSolverInternal.hpp` is `@surface internal` in `namespace slide::core::detail`, already included by both TUs (`PackSolver.cpp:7`, `PackSolverIterative.cpp:14`), and includes only `PackSolver.hpp` (public) and `Numeric.hpp` (`@surface support`) — internal→support is the permitted direction, so no api/support header ends up including an internal one.

THE ONE THING THE REVIEWER MISSED, and it is a correctness hazard, not a style point. `cmake/SlideCoreTarget.cmake:49-51` exempts only `ForwardSensitivity.cpp` and `PackSolverValidation.cpp` via `slide_use_strict_fp` — BOTH solver TUs compile under `cmake/StandardProjectSettings.cmake:58-59` `-Ofast -ffast-math` (and `/fp:fast` on MSVC). `Numeric.hpp:31-33` warns exactly against the proposed signature: "Clang can otherwise attach `nofpclass` to a by-value argument and fold even an integer bit-cast classification to true under -ffinite-math-only (part of -Ofast)." Today `voltage` is a local passed straight to `is_finite(const real_t &)` with no function-parameter boundary, so no `nofpclass` can be attributed. The proposed `real_t drop` by value introduces one, and after inlining clang may fold the finiteness gate to true — silently deleting the solver's validation. Fix the signature to `const real_t &`.

title: The failed-source-stepping rollback is unreachable from any test, and nothing asserts how far step() actually advances time
proposal:
Two short gate tests in tests/unit/core_PackSolver_test.cpp / core_PackStepper_test.cpp:

1. TEST_CASE("failed source stepping restores the last accepted solve") -- ScriptedAffineBatch whose OCV oscillates between two values so no fixed point exists; solve() once with a loose tolerance to publish a solution, record cell_current/node_voltage/terminal_voltage and diagnostics; then solve(nonzero, sparse_newton, 1e-15, 2) and assert Status::Numerical_failure with all three solution fields bit-identical to the recorded ones. Add the diagnostics equality assertion once the rollback finding above is fixed -- it is the falsifier for it.

2. TEST_CASE("step(substeps=n) advances exactly n*dt") -- an analytic roundtrip rather than fixture replay: run stepper A with step(I, 0, dt, {}, ladder, tol, 3), and stepper B on an identical freshly built pack with solveElectrical(I, ladder) followed by three step(I, k*dt, dt, ..., 1) calls that skip re-solving is not expressible, so instead assert the weaker invariant that A's final state equals B's after three single-substep calls at times 0, dt, 2*dt when the electrical solution is frozen (batch currents identical). Assert std::memcmp over state().raw() == 0. This pins the contract the parameter name currently denies.

verdict.reason:
CODE EXISTS AS QUOTED. PackSolver.cpp:406-415 is verbatim: "if (status == slide::Status::Success) { diagnostics_.source_steps = source_steps; return status; }" then "std::copy(rollback_cell_current_.begin(), ...)". PackStepper.cpp:281 is "for (int substep = 0; substep < substeps; ++substep)". PackStepper.hpp:33 confirms the 7th parameter is "int substeps = 1", so the trailing 10 at core_PackStepper_test.cpp:269 is substeps=10 -- the reviewer read the signature correctly.

HEADLINE REFUTED: "unreachable from any test" is FALSE. tests/unit/core_ModeC_test.cpp:258-281 ("Mode C cannot converge on update stagnation while KCL is violated") does reach it: line 273 "REQUIRE(solver.setRelaxationGain(1e-20) == Status::Success);" then line 274 "REQUIRE(solver.solve(1.0, core::PackSolveMode::relaxation, 1e-12, 2) != Status::Success);". PackSolverValidation.cpp:17-21 shows public solve() passes allow_source_stepping=true, and applied_current=1.0 != 0.0, so line 389 is entered. solveRelaxation returns Success every iteration (all values finite; PackSolverIterative.cpp:157-165 applies correction = relaxation_alpha_ * difference ~ 4e-20), but constraint_converged is false because diagnostics_.constraint_drift is ~4 -- the test itself asserts this at line 276 "REQUIRE(solver.diagnostics().constraint_drift > 1e-6);". So the loop exhausts and the rollback block executes. The reviewer's grep missed it because it asserts "!= Status::Success", not "== Numerical_failure". The reviewer's evidence sentence "The only Numerical_failure assertion in the owned tests is ... :809" is therefore a grep artifact, and the claim that nothing else "reaches line 389" is wrong.

RESIDUAL GAP IS STILL REAL (why I answer real=true). ModeC LINE-covers the rollback but cannot FALSIFY it. The first inner call at PackSolver.cpp:397, solveImpl(0.0, relaxation, 1e-12, 2, false), itself exhausts (same 1e-20 gain, constraint_drift ~4 against a 1e-12 bound) and returns Numerical_failure with allow_source_stepping=false, so the loop at 398 never runs and solution_ is never overwritten (solution_ is written only at 377-379 on convergence). Lines 411-413 thus copy back byte-identical values -- a no-op -- and ModeC:278-280 passes with or without the block. Line 414 "has_solution_ = rollback_has_solution" is observable only via a later solve's warm start (308-315), and ModeC ends at 281. Deleting 411-415 keeps the suite green.

PROPOSAL #1 AS WRITTEN IS A DUPLICATE, NOT A FALSIFIER. Its assertion set ("all three solution fields bit-identical to the recorded ones") already exists verbatim at ModeC_test.cpp:278-280, and it inherits the same defect: unless an INTERMEDIATE source step succeeds and overwrites solution_, the copies are a no-op. The proposal never states that requirement. (Its named fixture does exist -- ScriptedAffineBatch at core_PackSolver_test.cpp:99, used at 759.)

PROPOSAL #2 IS TECHNICALLY WRONG. stepImpl calls solver_.solve once (PackStepper.cpp:254) and topology_.thermal.assemble once (line 268) BEFORE the substep loop at 281; only the batch stepper calls are repeated. Three separate step() calls re-solve AND re-assemble cell_external_heat_ from updated cell_temperature_ (263-265) each time, so A != B on any thermal pack. core_PackStepper_test.cpp:133-139 already loops four single-substep step() calls on a thermal pack (options ".thermal = true", boundary{295.0}), which is exactly the B side -- the proposed memcmp would fail by construction. The proposal half-admits this ("skip re-solving is not expressible") and then asserts equality anyway.

SUBSTEPS HALF FULLY CONFIRMED. Grep for "substeps" across tests/ returns zero hits; core_PackStepper_test.cpp has 7 step( calls (80, 90, 134, 213, 269, 343, 365) and only 269 passes a 7th argument; grep for PackStepper in tests/integration/ returns "No matches found". Nothing anywhere asserts the elapsed time or the state reached for substeps>1.

CONTRACTS: PLAN.md sections 1.1-1.3 opened. Adding test cases touches no hot path -- no PC-1 per-step allocation, no PC-2 per-cell virtual dispatch, no PC-5 std::function in inner loops, no PC-10 physics-formula duplication (no formula is restated; the revised test reuses EulerLegacy directly). MC-4 "Tests mirror source names" is satisfied by landing in core_PackSolver_test.cpp / core_PackStepper_test.cpp. Minor note only: MC-1's "~700 lines is a review smell" is already exceeded by core_PackSolver_test.cpp (>1170 lines), so additions should be tight, but that pre-exists and is not caused by this proposal. Behaviour-preserving is trivially true: tests-only, no production numerics touched, no reassociation. (Caveat: proposal #1's parenthetical "add the diagnostics equality assertion once the rollback finding above is fixed" refers to a DIFFERENT finding; applying that fix would change observable diagnostics_ output and must be judged separately.)
verdict.revised_proposal:
Keep the finding but restate it as "executed yet unfalsifiable", not "unreachable", and cite core_ModeC_test.cpp:258-281 as prior art in both the finding and any new test's comment.

1. Rollback test -- make it a falsifier, not a third copy of ModeC:278-280. The test must force at least one INNER source step to succeed so solution_ is genuinely overwritten before a later step fails; otherwise lines 411-413 are a no-op and the test proves nothing. Using ScriptedAffineBatch (core_PackSolver_test.cpp:99), script the OCV sequence so the applied_current=0.0 solve and the low-fraction steps (1/8, 2/8) converge but a later fraction diverges. Then assert: (a) Status::Numerical_failure; (b) cell_current/node_voltage/terminal_voltage equal the values recorded BEFORE the failing solve -- which now differ from the last inner solve's published values, so the assertion bites; (c) a subsequent solve of the original current converges warm, which is the only way to pin line 414 (has_solution_ = rollback_has_solution). Verify falsification by commenting out 411-415 and confirming the new test goes red -- without that check it is another green no-op. Do NOT bundle the diagnostics equality assertion here; diagnostics_ is legitimately clobbered by the recursive solveImpl reset at line 317 and belongs to the separate diagnostics finding.

2. Stepper test -- drop the A-vs-three-step() roundtrip; it is false on any thermal pack. Assert the advance directly against the integrator instead: build a NON-thermal pack (so cell_external_heat_ is never written, PackStepper.cpp:271-279 skipped), call solveElectrical once to freeze current_density_, then compare stepper.step(I, t0, dt, {}, ladder, tol, n) against n direct EulerLegacy::step calls on an identically built batch at times t0, t0+dt, ..., t0+(n-1)*dt with that same frozen current density, asserting std::memcmp over state().raw() == 0. That pins both the substep COUNT and the time argument (time + substep*dt, PackStepper.cpp:289/294) -- the two things currently unasserted -- without assuming an equivalence the code does not provide. Add a negative companion asserting step(..., substeps=0) == Status::Invalid_parameters (guarded at PackStepper.cpp:244), which is also currently untested. Separately, document in PackStepper.hpp whether the caller is expected to advance its own clock by n*dt after a substeps=n call; the header currently states no contract, which is the root of the ambiguity.

verdict.reason:
Verified verbatim at both sites. PackTopology.cpp:180-187 "adjacency[branch.node_positive].push_back(branch.node_negative); ... sparsity.emplace_back(std::min(branch.node_positive, branch.node_negative), std::max(...))" is textually identical to :395-402 modulo the name expected_sparsity; the sort/unique pair at :188-189 matches :410-413; the BFS at :192-204 (seen) matches :417-429 (visited). One helper suffices with no flags: I checked lines 205-330 and the plain adjacency is dead after :204 -- ladder detection uses a separate simple_adjacency (:217, :222-223, :228-234, :241).

The arbiter objection fails, and the sparsity check is still load-bearing for the other caller. SolverWorkspace::configure builds the Eigen pattern straight from the stored field (PackSolver.cpp:184-190: "for (const auto &[node_a, node_b] : netlist.nodal_sparsity) { ... triplets.emplace_back(a, b, 1.0); ... }"), so a stored pattern disagreeing with the branches is exactly the "solver was never given" failure. Under sharing the helper is the definition of "implied by branches" and the stored field is still independent data, so the comparison at :414 stays real. In the self-check path at :513-517 the check is already tautological today because the two copies are identical text, so factoring costs nothing. The project's genuine independent arbiter is elsewhere: .claude/summaries/handoff-2026-07-10-p9b-parser-fuzz.md:21 -- "The netlist oracle does not call `validateElectricalNetlist`. It independently proves cell/path/location bijection, endpoints/resistors, connectivity, sparsity, ladder classification/orientation, and imported thermal metadata."

Digit-identical is trivial: there is zero floating-point arithmetic in the duplicated region -- no summation to reassociate, no FMA. The only double is branch.resistance in the comparison at :389 "if (!(is_finite(branch.resistance) && branch.resistance > 0.0))", which stays in the validator switch. BFS order is unchanged anyway (identical adjacency insertion order) and only the all-visited predicate is consumed; all_of(!=0) is equivalent to !any_of(==0).

No contract violated. PC-10 is "ONE physics source: every formula exists in exactly one scalar-generic definition" (PLAN.md:164) -- graph derivation is not physics, and PLAN.md:30 generalizes it ("Never write the same fact twice (PC-10)"), so the proposal aligns with the contract. PC-1 ("ZERO heap allocations per accepted simulation step", PLAN.md:155) is untouched: both sites are cold -- configure does make_unique plus analyzePattern, and the derivation already allocates a vector<vector<uint32_t>>. Helpers land in the .cpp anonymous namespace, so D-42/MC-5 ("no api or support header may include an internal one") is unaffected. MC-1 improves: 642 lines minus ~30.

CAVEAT the proposal gets wrong: it says replace "lines 395-402/410-433" with the two calls. Lines 395-402 are INSIDE the per-branch loop whose guard at :375-378 ("if (branch.node_positive >= netlist.node_count || branch.node_negative >= netlist.node_count || branch.node_positive == branch.node_negative) return slide::Status::Invalid_parameters;") is the only thing making adjacency[branch.node_positive] safe. buildBranchGraph indexes unguarded, so calling it there or earlier is an out-of-bounds vector write on a public entry point -- PackSolver.hpp:4 is "@surface api" and configure at :108 takes a caller-supplied CompiledElectricalNetlist. The tests would not catch it: tests/unit/core_PackTopology_test.cpp:238-290 covers sparsity/ladder shape/ladder node/ladder range/zero resistance/missing cell/disconnected but never passes the validator an out-of-range node; the one out-of-range mutation at :314 (pack.electrical.branches[0].node_positive = node_count) goes through finalizeImportedTopology, which pre-checks bounds at :496-500, so neither it nor the NetlistCsv fuzzer reaches the validator with a bad index.

title: Ladder detection does a linear find_if over all branches per cell -- O(cells^2) inside documented input bounds (~10^10 ops for a legal 2.4 MiB CSV)

verdict.reason:
The quoted code exists verbatim and means what the reviewer says. PackTopology.cpp:255-268 is exactly as quoted: the `std::find_if` over `netlist.branches` sits inside `for (const auto cell : cells)`, which sits inside the `while (current != netlist.terminal_negative)` layer walk opened at :240. Total work is sum over layers of (cells_in_layer * O(branches)) = O(branches^2). The three-line rollback `netlist.ladder_offsets.clear(); netlist.ladder_cells.clear(); netlist.ladder_nodes.clear();` appears verbatim at :246-248, :262-264, and :507-509. CONFIRMED.

Reachability CONFIRMED, and it is the load-bearing thing the reviewer did not verify, so I did. The ladder walk is gated at :211-215 on `std::any_of(... branch.kind != ElectricalBranchKind::cell ...)` -- any non-cell branch returns early. NetlistCsv.cpp shows V rows push `.kind = ElectricalBranchKind::cell` (:451-454), R rows push `.kind = ElectricalBranchKind::resistor` (:457-460), and the I row only assigns `candidate.electrical.terminal_positive = positive;` (:463) WITHOUT pushing a branch. So the reviewer's "V rows + one I row" CSV yields an all-cell branch list, clears the :211-215 gate, and reaches the quadratic walk. NetlistCsv.hpp:39 confirms the bound verbatim: "Input is bounded to 4 MiB, 100,000 rows, 32 columns, and 65,536 bytes/field." A 99,999-row series string is ~2.4 MiB, inside every bound.

One arithmetic correction: the headline says "~10^10 ops", the body says "~5x10^9". The body is right. For a pure series string, branches are in CSV order, so the find_if for layer k scans ~k entries; the sum is N^2/2 ~ 5x10^9 for N=99,999, not 10^10. The headline overstates by 2x. Not disqualifying; the nesting claim is what matters and it is certain.

NOT behaviour-preserving AS WRITTEN -- proposal (a) introduces an out-of-bounds read. There is no floating-point arithmetic anywhere in this function (pure integer index bookkeeping), so reassociation is a non-issue. The defect is different. The reviewer correctly identified that `branch.cell` is unvalidated at this point -- finalizeImportedPackTopology:496-500 checks only `branch.node_positive`/`node_negative`, never `branch.cell`, and the real bounds test `if (branch.cell >= cell_count ...)` lives at PackTopology.cpp:381 inside validateElectricalNetlist, which runs at :514 AFTER compileElectricalMetadata at :513. But having identified the hazard, the reviewer put the guard in the wrong loop: `candidate.cell < branch_of_cell.size()` guards the TABLE BUILD, while the query `branch_of_cell[cell]` is unguarded. `cell` comes from `layers`, populated by `cells.push_back(branch.cell)` at :225 with no filtering, so an out-of-range `branch.cell` reaches the query and indexes a `std::vector` out of bounds. The existing `find_if` never does this. That is UB introduced by the "digit-identical" refactor.

Proposal (b) checks out. I verified the entry-state invariant the reviewer relied on implicitly: the ladder vectors are empty on entry on both call paths (:629 compiles into a fresh `context.result`; :513 is preceded by the explicit clear at :507-509), so the early returns at :215/:230/:234 -- which currently leave the vectors untouched -- are equivalent to `return false` plus an unconditional clear at the call site. The reviewer's signature is however incomplete: `detectSeriesParallelLadder(CompiledElectricalNetlist &, const CompiledPackTopology &)` omits `node_count`, which the body needs both to size `simple_adjacency(node_count)` (:217) and as the `previous = node_count` sentinel (:238).

No contract violation. PLAN.md §1.1 preamble is explicit: "the user-facing API may be arbitrarily pleasant because it runs once at setup; after compile()/build(), only spans, indices, and precompiled kernels exist." compileElectricalMetadata is cold -- called only from compilePackDescription (:629) and finalizeImportedPackTopology (:513) -- so PC-1 ("ZERO heap allocations per accepted simulation step") does not reach it, and the function already allocates a std::map, a vector<vector>, and a std::queue. PC-8 forbids O(n^2) in the pack SOLVE, not compile, so the finding is aligned with it rather than governed by it. PC-10 is untouched (no physics formula here). MC-5 is fine -- the helper is file-local in the anonymous namespace. I also checked tests/unit/core_ParserAllocation_test.cpp since it includes NetlistCsv.hpp: its CSV injections are size-keyed (`FailAllocationOfSize failure{ 37U * sizeof(core::CompiledCell), 0, true }` at :1103), not global-occurrence-keyed, so a new 4*N-byte allocation will not perturb them.

Not already done, no pre-existing test: grep for "ladder" across tests/ hits core_PackTopology_test.cpp only at :33-34 (a 2x4 happy-path shape assertion, `ladder_offsets == {0,4,8}`) and :241-248 (validator mutation arms). Nothing covers scale or the quadratic path.
verdict.revised_proposal:
Keep both parts, with three fixes.

(a) Guard the QUERY, not just the table build. Add to the loop body:

  const auto slot = cell < branch_of_cell.size() ? branch_of_cell[cell] : no_branch;
  if (slot == no_branch || netlist.branches[slot].node_positive != current
      || netlist.branches[slot].node_negative != next)
    return false;

Treating an out-of-range `cell` as not-found is observably equivalent to the current find_if even though it takes a different in-function path, and this is worth stating explicitly rather than assuming. Today find_if WOULD locate a branch carrying an out-of-range cell id, and could match its endpoints and push it into ladder_cells. But that can only happen on the import path, where validateElectricalNetlist:381 (`branch.cell >= cell_count`) rejects the topology unconditionally at :514, and finalizeImportedPackTopology returns that Status; NetlistCsv.hpp:38 guarantees "output is unchanged on every non-Success result". So both paths return Invalid_parameters and neither publishes state. The returned Status and the published topology are identical; only the discarded intermediate differs. Do NOT instead size the table by max(cell)+1 -- `branch.cell` is an unvalidated uint32 there, so that is a 16 GB allocation on hostile input.

Also make the build loop index with std::size_t and cast, not `std::uint32_t b`, so a branches.size() above UINT32_MAX cannot wrap into an infinite loop:

  for (std::size_t b = 0; b < netlist.branches.size(); ++b) { ... branch_of_cell[candidate.cell] = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(b); }

and drop the `candidate.kind == ElectricalBranchKind::cell` test only because :211-215 has already returned for any non-cell branch -- that reasoning is sound, keep it in a comment so the coupling is not silently re-broken.

(b) Correct the helper signature to carry node_count:

  [[nodiscard]] bool detectSeriesParallelLadder(CompiledElectricalNetlist &netlist, const CompiledPackTopology &pack, std::uint32_t node_count);

turn the bailouts at :245-250 and :260-266 into `return false;`, and clear once at the call site. The empty-on-entry invariant that makes this equivalent holds on both call paths (:629 fresh, :513 pre-cleared) -- record it as a comment on the helper, since the equivalence depends on it. Leave :507-509 alone; it is a reset-before-recompile, a different concern.

Gate: this is an integer-only change with no FP, so the correct evidence is a digit-identical diff of the compiled topology on the existing fixtures -- assert `ladder_offsets`, `ladder_cells`, `ladder_nodes`, and `series_parallel_ladder` unchanged on the 2x4 case at core_PackTopology_test.cpp:33-34 and on every mutation arm at :241-248. Add the missing scale test the grep shows does not exist: a ~10^5-cell series CSV, with a wall-clock band registered BEFORE the run. Run it under ASan to prove the out-of-bounds query is actually closed -- that is the one claim I most expect a careless application of this fix to get wrong.

title: assignBatchLocations keys three separate std::maps on the same archetype string and mixes at()/operator[] access

verdict.reason: Code is verbatim-exact at PackTopology.cpp:152-172: three function-local std::maps ("std::map<std::string, std::uint32_t> batches; std::map<std::string, bool> thermal; std::map<std::string, std::uint32_t> next_lane;") all keyed on cell.archetype, with the at()/operator[] split on lines 169-170 ("batches.at(cell.archetype)" vs "next_lane[cell.archetype]++"). None escape the function. Not already done, not a false positive. No PC/MC/EC violation: PLAN.md:149-151 states the split explicitly -- "the user-facing API may be arbitrarily pleasant because it runs once at setup; after compile()/build(), only spans, indices, and precompiled kernels exist. Strings, maps, options dicts, nested constructors, parameter lookup -- all cold path, all gone before the first step." Both call sites (PackTopology.cpp:503 in finalizeImportedPackTopology, :627 in compilePackDescription) are cold compile, so PC-1/PC-2/PC-4/PC-5 do not bite; no physics formula is touched (PC-10 clear); the file is 643 lines and shrinks (MC-1 clear). Digit-identical holds trivially -- the function computes only std::uint32_t and bool, there is no floating-point arithmetic to reassociate -- and iteration order is preserved because std::less<> on std::string forwards to the same operator< as std::less<std::string>, so batch indices, batch_archetypes push order, and per-archetype lane numbers are unchanged. The thermal-disagreement early return is preserved bit-for-bit (first insert seeds thermal, later cells compare and return false at the same cell, with batch_archetypes still untouched), and that branch is already covered by tests/unit/core_PackTopology_test.cpp:316-318, the "mixed batch physics" mutator: "pack.cells[1].archetype = pack.cells[0].archetype; pack.cells[1].thermal = true;". TWO CORRECTIONS to the reviewer's write-up. (a) The severity rationale is inflated: the claim that operator[] "silently default-inserts, which reads as if a missing archetype were legal" misreads the code -- next_lane is declared at :156 and touched at exactly one site, :170, so the default-insert IS the lane-counter initialisation, not a swallowed lookup failure. There is no "missing archetype" failure story on that map, hence no "two different failure stories on the same line". The real justification is narrower and still sufficient: three red-black trees, three string copies and three node allocations per archetype, and three places to keep in sync. (b) The proposal itself regresses one thing -- it swaps checked at() for unchecked find(...)->second, trading away a bound for nothing, and std::less<> buys no heterogeneous lookup because every lookup key is already a std::string.

title: CompiledThermalGraph::assemble runs once per pack step but is not noexcept, and the header brief advertises the whole file as cold
evidence:
PackTopology.hpp:3 -- the MC-3 contract line:
 * @brief Value-semantic pack combinators and cold-compiled electrical/thermal topology.

PackTopology.hpp:135-138 -- the one member of this header that is not cold:
  [[nodiscard]] slide::Status assemble(std::span<const real_t> cell_temperature,

proposal:
(a) Mark assemble `noexcept` on both declaration and definition. It is correct and free: the body indexes pre-sized std::vectors and std::spans with operator[], calls std::fill/std::copy over existing storage, and returns Status -- there is no allocation and no throwing call anywhere between PackTopology.cpp:535 and 617. Since it sits on the per-step path this also makes PC-1/PC-4 (zero per-step allocations, no exceptions on the hot path) machine-checkable rather than a claim in prose: a future allocation added to the body becomes a terminate rather than a silent contract violation.

(b) Amend the MC-3 brief so the hot/cold split is stated where a reader looks for it, e.g. `@brief Value-semantic pack combinators, cold-compiled topology, and the per-step thermal assembly (PLAN.md D-21; compile cold, assemble()  hot).` The current wording tells a reader the file is entirely cold, which is exactly the assumption under which someone adds a std::map or a diagnostic string to assemble().

No numeric behaviour change; `noexcept` alters only std::is_nothrow_* traits, which nothing in the tree queries for this type.

verdict.reason:

The noexcept claim survives inspection. I read the whole body (PackTopology.cpp:535-617): size/finiteness guards returning Status, a non-capturing-by-value lambda, indexing of pre-sized std::vector/std::span via operator[], `std::fill(trial_edge_incidence...)`, `std::copy(trial_edge_flux..., edge_flux.begin())`, and `std::numeric_limits<std::size_t>::max()` (constexpr). `is_finite` is already `noexcept` (Numeric.hpp:29, :39). `real_t` is `double` (StateArena.hpp:34), so no user-defined throwing arithmetic. Grep for `assemble` across src/ and tests/ shows only direct calls (PackStepper.cpp:268 and tests/unit/core_PackTopology_test.cpp:93,121,145,170,351,359,364,389,402,420) — the address is never taken, never stored in std::function, and no `is_nothrow_*` trait is queried, so adding noexcept cannot change overload resolution or break a caller. Digit-identical: no arithmetic is touched, no summation order changes.

Two corrections to the reviewer's rationale, which is materially oversold:

(1) "a future allocation added to the body becomes a terminate" is FALSE. `noexcept` traps throws, not allocations. A `std::map` insert or a diagnostic `std::string` added to `assemble` allocates and returns normally; nothing terminates. noexcept makes PC-4 (no exceptions) partly runtime-checkable; it does nothing for PC-1.

(2) PC-1 on this exact path is ALREADY machine-checked, so the "rather than a claim in prose" framing is wrong. tests/unit/core_P2G1_allocation_test.cpp:76 is `TEST_CASE("P2-G1 coupled thermal pack step allocates nothing", "[core][pack][thermal][allocation][P2-G1]")`, building `parallel(2, cell({.archetype="spm", .thermal=true}))` with `.thermal_links = {{"p00","p01",2.0}}` (a real edge, so assemble does work) and asserting `REQUIRE(after == before)` around `stepper.step(20.0, 0.1, 0.1)` (lines 100-105). PLAN.md:155 lists PC-1 as "enforced by counting-allocator asserts" — that enforcement is present here.

On part (b): the brief is weaker evidence than claimed. Read strictly, "cold-compiled electrical/thermal topology" says the topology is produced by a cold compile — which is true — not that every member is cold; "advertises the whole file as cold" is an aggressive reading. It is still a genuine MC-3 gap: PLAN.md:184 requires "Every `src/core` header opens with a 3-6 line contract comment: what it owns, which PLAN.md § it implements, hot/cold classification", and the current 4-line comment names no PLAN.md § and omits the one hot member. Note the established pattern is inconsistent (AgeingModelMask.hpp and BatchBuilder.hpp carry the full form; AsyncRecorder.hpp, CellDesign.hpp, Dual.hpp, PackStepper.hpp carry only @brief + @surface), so this is hygiene, not a regression.

No PC/MC/EC contract is violated by the change. There is no `-fno-exceptions` flag in CMakeLists.txt or cmake/, and no noexcept policy in .claude/cpp-style.md, develop/conventions.md, or PLAN.md, so this is a local improvement rather than enforcement of a written rule.

title: failSemantic returns a bool that all eight call sites discard, and never sets the offset its own header documents
proposal:
(a) Change the return type to slide::Status:

  [[nodiscard]] slide::Status failSemantic(NetlistCsvDiagnostic &diagnostic, std::size_t row,
                                           std::string_view message)
  { diagnostic.row = row; diagnostic.message.assign(message); return slide::Status::Invalid_parameters; }

Each of the eight sites becomes a single `return failSemantic(diagnostic, row, "...");` -- 16 lines to 8, the discarded-value smell disappears, and it becomes impossible to add a ninth site that reports a diagnostic and then returns Success. The [[nodiscard]] enforces that. Signature note: it stays consistent with the lexicon (`valid.../is...` returns bool, and this is neither); CsvReader::fail keeps its bool because that one IS consumed as a boolean by CsvReader::next.

(b) Either set `diagnostic.offset` in failSemantic (the parser does not retain a byte offset per element, so the honest value is the row's start offset, which would need CsvReader to expose it), or amend NetlistCsv.hpp:27 to `//!< source byte at or immediately after a grammar failure; zero for semantic failures`. Right now the comment contradicts the code for the eight most common rejections, which is the failure mode a user debugging a rejected CSV hits first. Documenting is the low-risk option and changes no behaviour.

title: assemble() has no exact analytic oracle: the isothermal limit (every heat exactly zero) is untested

verdict.reason:

PackTopology.cpp:566-572 reads verbatim: "const real_t difference = temperature(edge.high) - temperature(edge.low); ... const real_t flux = edge.conductance * difference;". core_PackTopology_test.cpp:89-98 matches the quoted block character-for-character (REQUIRE(q_ext[0] == 30.0); REQUIRE(q_ext[1] == -70.0); REQUIRE(boundary_heat[0] == 40.0);).

Gap confirmed by grep, not assumed. Grepping tests/ for "assemble(" returns exactly lines 93,121,145,170,351,359,364,389,402,420 of core_PackTopology_test.cpp and nothing elsewhere. I read all of them: 121/145 assert Invalid_states, 170/389/420 assert Invalid_parameters, 351 Invalid_parameters, 359/364/402 Invalid_states. Line 93 is the only Success-with-numbers case. Grep for "isotherm" across tests/ hits only archetype names ("a-isothermal", SpmComposition::isothermal) and PackStepper.cpp:191 "one archetype cannot mix thermal and isothermal lanes" — none is a zero-heat oracle. core_PackStepper_test.cpp:81-83 asserts cellExternalHeat()[0] == 20.0 / == -20.0 on a single-edge NON-isothermal pack. So no existing test covers the isothermal limit.

I re-derived the existing oracle to check the reviewer read the physics right: edges sort to (low=0,high=1,k=3.0) and (low=1,high=2,k=2.0); flux1 = 3.0*(310-300) = 30, flux2 = 2.0*(290-310) = -40; q_ext[0] = +30, q_ext[1] = -30 + (-40) = -70, boundary_heat[0] = -(-40) = +40. Matches. The reviewer's reading is accurate.

Exactness argument is sound. "real_t total{}" (line 579) is +0.0; flux = conductance * (T-T) = k * (+0.0) = +0.0 for finite k > 0 (line 564 already guarantees conductance > 0.0); contribution = sign * flux is +0.0 or -0.0; +0.0 + (-0.0) = +0.0 under round-to-nearest, so every endpoint total is bit-exactly +0.0 independent of incidence order, and "== 0.0" is true for both signed zeros. edge_flux is filled by std::copy at line 609 from trial_edge_flux, so it is all +0.0 too. edge_flux is a public member (PackTopology.hpp:130 "std::vector<real_t> edge_flux{}; //!< last successfully assembled edge fluxes"), so the assertion is reachable.

The reviewer's negative claim is also correct: global sum(q_ext)+sum(boundary_heat)==0.0 is not an exact oracle in general, because each endpoint total is a separately rounded incident-order sum and summing those reassociates.

Digit-identical: the proposal is a test-only addition; PackTopology.cpp is untouched, so no production number changes.

Contracts (PLAN.md 155-186): PC-1 (zero heap alloc per accepted step) is about the hot path — compilePackDescription is cold-path compile, as every existing test in this file already uses. verdict.reason:

Recorder.cpp:126-136 and AsyncRecordingCodec.cpp:439-449 match the reviewer's transcription character for character, including the `static_cast<std::size_t>(lanes_)` casts and line breaks. The helper performs NO floating-point arithmetic at all — two integer-indexed loads (`steps[index]`, `times[index]`) and two `subspan` offset/extent computations in `std::size_t`. There is no summation to reassociate, no loop to replace with `std::reduce`, no multiply-add to fuse. `real_t` values are copied bit-for-bit and the spans alias the same storage at the same offsets. Nothing in the FP-reassociation hazard class applies.

(4) NO PC/MC VIOLATION — and there is direct, documented precedent in this exact subsystem. PLAN.md:1243 (D-42) states the load-bearing rule as "**no api or support header may include an internal one**". The direction here is the permitted one: the new `detail/` header is internal and must include `../Recorder.hpp` (api, per its `@surface api` tag at Recorder.hpp:4) to see `SnapshotView` (defined Recorder.hpp:55-61) and `real_t`. `src/core/detail/AsyncRecordingFormat.hpp` already does precisely this — `#include "../AsyncRecorder.hpp"` at line 16, under `@surface internal` at line 11. title: BinaryRecording::open rejects any header whose correct CRC happens to be zero — a redundant clause that the async reader does not have
evidence:
RecordingFormat.cpp:371-373:
      || header.header_size != header_bytes || expected_crc == 0
      || crc32(std::as_bytes(std::span{ &crc_header, 1 })) != expected_crc

`expected_crc` is the CRC the writer stored (RecordingFormat.cpp:369). The clause rejects the file when that value is 0. But the very next clause already recomputes the CRC and demands equality, so `expected_crc == 0` rejects *precisely* the files whose correct CRC is 0 — roughly one written recording in 2^32, which `Recorder::writeBinary` will happily produce (RecordingFormat.cpp:337 sets whatever crc32 returns, with no check) and then never be able to open. A zero-filled placeholder header is already rejected by the magic check at :370 and by the recompute at :373, so the clause protects nothing.

The sibling reader of the sibling format has no such clause — AsyncRecordingCodec.cpp:275 is simply
      || header.header_crc32 != fileHeaderCrc(header)

Same file (:371) shows a second undocumented divergence: this reader accepts older minors (`header.minor > format_minor` rejects only newer), while AsyncRecordingCodec.cpp:273 demands exact equality (`header.minor != format_minor`). Two formats in one subsystem with opposite forward/backward-compatibility policies, neither commented.
proposal:
1. Delete `|| expected_crc == 0` at RecordingFormat.cpp:372. With the helper from finding `header-crc-helper` the whole check becomes `|| headerCrc(header) != header.header_crc32`, matching AsyncRecordingCodec.cpp:275 exactly. Behaviour change is confined to headers whose true CRC is 0: those go from "always rejected" to "accepted", which is the intended semantics.
2. Pick one minor-version policy and write it down in the format contract comment. If the `.slrec` intent is "minor bumps are backward compatible", then AsyncRecordingCodec.cpp:273 should also become `header.minor > format_minor`; if not, RecordingFormat.cpp:371 should become `!=`. Do not leave it implicit — a reader has to diff two files to discover which format tolerates what.
3. Add the gate: `TEST_CASE("a zero-valued header CRC is accepted when it is the correct CRC")` — craft a 64-byte header, brute-force the `snapshots` field until `headerCrc(header) == 0`, and REQUIRE that `BinaryRecording::open` returns Success rather than Invalid_parameters.

verdict.reason:
CODE CONFIRMED VERBATIM. RecordingFormat.cpp:369-373 reads exactly:
  const std::uint32_t expected_crc = std::exchange(crc_header.header_crc32, 0U);
  if (header.magic != recording_magic || header.major != format_major
      || header.minor > format_minor || header.endian != endian_marker
      || header.header_size != header_bytes || expected_crc == 0
      || crc32(std::as_bytes(std::span{ &crc_header, 1 })) != expected_crc
Truth table over the two clauses: (expected==0, recomputed==0) -> clause A rejects, clause B accepts; (expected==0, recomputed!=0) -> both reject; (expected!=0) -> A silent, B decides. So `expected_crc == 0` changes the verdict on EXACTLY the set {headers whose true CRC is 0} and nothing else. The reviewer's reading is correct.

title: IndexedPiecewiseLinear::eval and ::derivative duplicate the segment-locator, with the same guard written in two different operand orders


Both `else if` arms are identical (`< x_[i] && i > 0`). The two `raw_bin`/`bin` lines are the same expression modulo the local's name.

NOT A NUMERICALLY MEANINGFUL DIFFERENCE. Both operands are side-effect-free, so `A && B` == `B && A` here; the guards are logically equal regardless of any index invariant. The locator body is pure integer/comparison work over an unchanged FP expression `(x - x_.front()) * inv_bin_width_` — no reassociation, no FMA fusion, no summation reorder. It returns an index, so downstream interpolation is bit-identical.

ONE HELPER SUFFICES, NO FLAGS. The call sites differ only in the domain they feed it, not in the logic they need. eval returns early at :138/:140 so it reaches the locator only with `x_.front() < xp < x_.back()`; derivative instead CLAMPS at :165-168 and falls through, so it can call with `x == x_.front()` or `x == x_.back()`. The shared body already handles both: at `x == x_.back()`, `raw_bin` = bins, `std::min` clamps to `segment_.size()-1`, and the `++i` arm is blocked by `i + 1 < x_.size() - 1`. THE REVIEWER'S SAFETY PROOF IS FALSE — this is the one thing to fix. The proposal asserts build() at :119 "caps every stored index at `x.size() - 3`" and asks to write that into a comment. It does not. `while (segment_index + 1 < x.size() - 1 && ...) ++segment_index;` increments only when `segment_index < x.size() - 2`, so after the increment `segment_index <= x.size() - 2`. title: The constant-diffusivity admission test probes only x = 0, 0.5, 1, so any expression with those three roots passes as constant
proposal:
`p(x) = x*(x - 0.5)*(x - 1)` is exactly zero at all three probes, so the BPX string `"3.3e-14 + x*(x-0.5)*(x-1)"` -- entirely within the supported grammar (numbers, `x`, `*`, `-`, parens) -- is absorbed as the constant 3.3e-14 while being state-dependent everywhere else. Its magnitude at x=0.25 is 0.047, fourteen orders above the accepted value. Fix: probe at abscissae that are not the roots of any low-order symmetric polynomial the wire format is likely to carry, e.g.
```cpp
constexpr std::array sample_points{ 0.0, 0.2113248654051871, 0.5, 0.7886751345948129, 1.0 };
std::array<real_t, sample_points.size()> samples{};   // stop hard-coding 3
```
(the two interior points are the 2-point Gauss-Legendre nodes on [0,1]). This cannot make aliasing impossible -- no finite probe set can -- but it raises the required degree from 3 to 5 and removes the trivially-constructible case. Also fix the coupled literal: `std::array<real_t, 3>` at line 69 silently must track `sample_points` and today does so only by coincidence; `sample_points.size()` states the constraint. And name the `64.0` at line 74 (`constexpr real_t constant_probe_tolerance_ulps = 64.0;`) -- it is the only unexplained magnitude in the admission rule. behaviour_change: true only for expressions that are state-dependent but currently misread as constant; every existing fixture (a bare number, `"3.3e-14"`, `"3.3e-14*(2+2)/4"` at core_ParameterSet_test.cpp:445) is genuinely constant and still returns the identical double.

title: Three hand-rolled index loops state invariants that one standard algorithm or a two-line helper would state directly
proposal:
(a) ParameterCurve.hpp:29-33 becomes the two properties it actually asserts:
```cpp
  const auto finite = [](real_t v) { return is_finite(v); };
  return std::ranges::all_of(curve.stoichiometry, finite)
      && std::ranges::all_of(curve.value, finite)
      && std::ranges::adjacent_find(curve.stoichiometry, std::ranges::greater_equal{})
           == curve.stoichiometry.end();   // strictly increasing
```
Same boolean, no side effects, and "strictly increasing" stops being an `i > 0` special case.
(b) Add a local helper in BpxParameterReader.cpp:
```cpp
[[nodiscard]] std::optional<std::vector<real_t>> numberArray(const JsonValue &value);
// nullopt unless value.kind == array and every element is a number; reserves array.size()
```
Then `jsonCurve` reads `auto xs = numberArray(x->second); auto ys = numberArray(y->second); if (!xs || !ys || xs->size() != ys->size()) return std::nullopt; curve = { std::move(*xs), std::move(*ys) };` -- the size equality is checked once, in one place, and the two `push_back` loops (which currently grow both vectors without reserving) become two reserved fills.
