title: Nine unexplained numeric literals govern the cycler's solvers, including one absolute tolerance applied to a user-supplied residual of unknown units
proposal:
Three distinct problems, all fixed by naming:
(a) Dimensional. 158, 187 and 284 compare a *current increment in amperes* against 1e-10, but 245 compares `residual` — the value returned by an arbitrary user ExperimentFunction, whose units are whatever the user chose — against the same 1e-10. A control written in mV instead of V converges 1000x too loosely, silently. This wants a relative criterion or, at minimum, `constexpr real_t custom_residual_tolerance = 1e-10; // absolute, in the caller's own units — see docs`.
(b) Unexplained magic. `3.7` at 175 is a nominal cell voltage used as a CP warm start; `100.0 * capacity_Ah()` at 229 is a 100C clamp; `7.0*24.0*3600.0` at 427 is the one-week runaway guard that produces the user-visible string "maximum step duration" (738-741) and is duplicated in the test at core_Experiment_test.cpp:1077. None is named or documented in Experiment.hpp. Introduce, in an anonymous namespace at the top of CyclerV2.cpp: `constexpr real_t nominal_cell_voltage_V = 3.7;`, `constexpr real_t maximum_c_rate = 100.0;`, `constexpr real_t unbounded_segment_horizon_s = 7.0 * 24.0 * 3600.0;` and reference the last one from Experiment.hpp's doc for TerminationReason::limit so callers can see it.
(c) Iteration caps 12 (150), 12 (176), 24 (231), 45 (626) are four bare loop bounds; the 45 in particular encodes "bisect a double interval to the last bit" and deserves `constexpr int event_bisection_iterations = 45; // 2^-45 of a step, below double round-off on typical dt`. All (b) and (c) are pure renames of the same constants — digit-identical.

verdict.reason:
Every quoted line exists verbatim. src/core/CyclerV2.cpp:150 `for (int iteration = 0; iteration < 12; ++iteration) {`; :158 `if (std::abs(next - current) <= 1e-10) {`; :175 `current = signed_power / 3.7;`; :176 `for (int iteration = 0; iteration < 12; ++iteration) {`; :184 `if (!(is_finite(derivative) && std::abs(derivative) > 1e-12))`; :187 `if (std::abs(next - current) <= 1e-10) {`; :229 `const real_t maximum_current = 100.0 * batch_->capacity_Ah();`; :231 `for (int iteration = 0; iteration < 24; ++iteration) {`; :245 `if (std::abs(residual) <= 1e-10)`; :279 `if (!(is_finite(derivative) && std::abs(derivative) > 1e-14))`; :284 `if (std::abs(next - current) <= 1e-10) {`; :427 `real_t horizon = duration > 0.0 ? duration : 7.0 * 24.0 * 3600.0;`; :626 `for (int iteration = 0; iteration < 45; ++iteration) {`.

The dimensional claim holds. :284 compares `next - current`, both amperes (clamped by `maximum_current`), while :245 compares `residual`, the return of `segment.custom_control` — an arbitrary user `ExperimentFunction` (:237-242, value produced at :206-210). Two different quantities against the identical literal 1e-10. Confirmed.

The 1e-12 (:184) vs 1e-14 (:279) split is also real and both are singularity floors on a `derivative`, but note they are NOT the same quantity: :184 guards d(power)/d(current) = `voltage - resistance[0]*current` (units W/A = V); :279 guards a finite-difference d(residual)/d(current) in user-units/A. Different units, so a single shared floor would be wrong — name them separately, do not unify.

The linkage claims check out: :427's horizon is the only path to :738-741 `} else if (duration <= 0.0 && !cut_by_schedule) { solution.reason = TerminationReason::limit; ... solution.termination_name = "maximum step duration";`, asserted at tests/unit/core_Experiment_test.cpp:1079 `CHECK(output.termination_name == "maximum step duration");` with the same literal at :1077 `cycler.run(unbounded_event, 7.0 * 24.0 * 3600.0, output)`. `grep -n "TerminationReason" -A3 src/core/Experiment.hpp` shows :92-95 as bare enumerators with no doc comment, so "not documented in Experiment.hpp" is confirmed. `grep -rni "nominal.*volt|v_nominal|voltage_nominal" src/` returns nothing, so 3.7 is not a duplicated fact and PC-10 does not bite. The 100.0 is genuinely a C-rate: :449-451 shows `value_is_c_rate ? segment.value * batch_->capacity_Ah() : segment.value` yielding amperes, same construction.

Digit-identity: `grep -rn "using real_t" src/` gives src/core/StateArena.hpp:34 `using real_t = double;`. Every literal keeps its exact double bits under `constexpr real_t`, no float narrowing, no summation reassociation, no FMA fusion, and `7.0*24.0*3600.0` is exact in binary under any association (7*24=168, 168*3600=604800). An anonymous namespace already exists at :26-69 to host them. Digit-identical — for the NAMING variant only (see revised_proposal).

Contracts: I read PLAN.md §1.1-1.3. `constexpr` constants add no heap allocation (PC-1), no dispatch (PC-2), no `std::function` (PC-5), no header include (MC-5), no duplicated formula (PC-10). MC-1 is bookkeeping, not a violation: PLAN.md §8 line 1797 records "`CyclerV2.cpp` is a reviewed 771-line MC-1 cohesion exception to preserve the frozen non-IPO runner transaction" and `wc -l` confirms exactly 771; line 1800 re-affirms it as one of only two justified `src/core` files over 700. Adding ~10 lines requires updating that §8 number, nothing more. My strongest refutation angle — that line shifts would break the frozen M0.3 exact-coverage hashes — FAILS: all six pinned `site_id`s in tests/coverage/status_failure_exceptions.json are `src/core/PackSolver.cpp:{351,588,652,796,887}` and `src/core/SpectralModel.hpp:314`; none is in CyclerV2.cpp.

TWO REVIEWER ERRORS I am not endorsing. (1) The failure narrative is INVERTED. "A control written in mV instead of V converges 1000x too loosely" is backwards: residual_mV = 1000*residual_V, so |residual| <= 1e-10 demands |residual_V| <= 1e-13, which is 1000x TIGHTER, not looser. The reviewer also missed that the loop does not fail when the residual test is too tight — it falls through to the dimensionally-sound ampere criterion at :284, which returns Success on step stagnation. So the real hazard is the OPPOSITE scaling (a residual normalized or expressed in large units) firing :245 at iteration 0 and returning Success with the unmodified incoming `current` — a silent wrong answer, not a silent loose one. (2) "the 45 in particular encodes 'bisect a double interval to the last bit'" is FALSE: double has 52 mantissa bits, so reaching the last bit of a bracket of width dt needs ~52-53 halvings; 45 is 7-8 bits short.

title: drive_cycle is the only control mode omitted from the post-advance re-evaluation, so its reported current lags the reported time by one step
proposal: Failure scenario, from the project's own fixture: core_Experiment_test.cpp:550-581 registers US06 with time {0, 0.5, 1.0}, current {1.0, -1.0, 0.0} and samples at 0.25 s. The last accepted sub-step starts at local_time 0.75, where driveCurrent interpolates to -0.5; that value is pushed alongside time 1.0, where the table says the current is 0.0. The test pins the lagged value: `CHECK(solution.current.back() == Catch::Approx(-0.5));`. Either reading is defensible — ZOH-at-left-endpoint is what is physically applied over the interval, interpolate-at-output-time is what PyBaMM reports — but the code currently does one thing for drive cycles and the opposite for the four other time-varying modes, and nothing says which is intended. Decide and write it down: either add `else if (segment.mode == ControlMode::drive_cycle) after_current = driveCurrent(*cycle, local_time + dt);` (behaviour change: the 9C-3 recorded hashes at core_Experiment_test.cpp:323-330 and the -0.5 assertion must be re-registered), or document the ZOH convention on ControlMode::drive_cycle in Experiment.hpp and add a comment at 459 saying the omission from the ladder is deliberate. Adopting the resolveControl helper (dup-control-resolve) with a `switch` over ControlMode makes this choice explicit and un-forgettable, since a switch over the enum can be made exhaustive.

verdict.reason:
The quoted code exists verbatim and means what the reviewer says. CyclerV2.cpp:459-460 is `} else if (segment.mode == ControlMode::drive_cycle) {` / `current = driveCurrent(*cycle, local_time);`. The post-advance ladder at 586-604 tests exactly `ControlMode::voltage`, `::power`, `::custom_explicit`, `::custom_implicit` and no drive_cycle; `real_t after_current = current;` at 585 is therefore left at the left-endpoint value and pushed at 721-724 against `time` already incremented by `accepted_dt` (719).

The arithmetic checks out. driveCurrent (310-321) is LINEAR INTERPOLATION, not a ZOH lookup: `const real_t fraction = (local_time - cycle.time[i]) / (cycle.time[i + 1] - cycle.time[i]); return cycle.current[i] + fraction * (cycle.current[i + 1] - cycle.current[i]);`. For the fixture at core_Experiment_test.cpp:550-553 (`.time = { 0.0, 0.5, 1.0 }, .current = { 1.0, -1.0, 0.0 }`) sampled at 0.25: the last sub-step starts at local_time 0.75, i=1, fraction=0.5, current = -1.0 + 0.5*(0.0 - -1.0) = -0.5, pushed with local time 1.0 where the table gives 0.0. The test pins it: `CHECK(solution.current.back() == Catch::Approx(-0.5));`, and the first drive sample is pinned the same way, `CHECK(solution.current[9] == Catch::Approx(1.0));` = driveCurrent(0). No documentation of the convention exists — grep over Experiment.hpp, src/api and docs/ returns only the enum entry (Experiment.hpp:28), the `std::string drive_cycle{}` field (64) and legacy v2 prose about `followCurrent`.

THREE CORRECTIONS, none fatal to the finding:

(1) "the only control mode omitted" is loose. `custom_differential` (the trailing `else` at 472-487) is also absent from the ladder, but defensibly so: line 483 `current += derivative * dt;` already forward-Eulers it to the right endpoint before advance(). Restated correctly: drive_cycle is the only mode whose REPORTED current is stale relative to the reported time. Substance stands.

(2) Not merely a reporting convention. `validSegment` (detail/ExperimentSemantics.hpp:128-131) rejects only an empty name for drive_cycle — `case ControlMode::drive_cycle: if (segment.drive_cycle.empty()) return false; break;` — and does NOT forbid `current_cutoff` or `custom_terminations` (the fuzz model at tests/fuzz/FuzzSupport.hpp:195-199 forbids them, but that constrains the corpus, not the API). A programmatically constructed drive_cycle segment with a cutoff or a current-reading custom termination feeds the stale `after_current` into `indicator(time + dt, local_time + dt, after_voltage, after_current, ...)` at 613-618, which forwards it to `evaluateFunction(termination.indicator, ..., event_current, ...)` at 527-532 and then roots on it in the bisection at 624-714. That is a state-changing defect, not cosmetic.

(3) The blast radius is bigger than stated. Line 605-606, `if (status == slide::Status::Success && after_current != current) status = voltageAt(after_current, after_voltage);` means the reported VOLTAGE array changes too, not only current (voltageAt at 138-145 is a pure observable — writes only `density_` scratch and `output` — so the state hash is untouched for event-free segments). Both the current and voltage components of the 9C-3 recorded hashes must be re-registered.

Not behaviour-preserving: the fix arm changes solution.current and solution.voltage by construction (9C-3 fixture "9c3-breakpoints", time {0,0.25,0.5}, current {0.25,-0.75,0.5}, sample_period 0.125: reported currents go from {0.25,-0.25,-0.75,-0.125} to {-0.25,-0.75,-0.125,0.5}). Only the documentation arm is digit-identical. No FP reassociation is involved — this is a semantic change, not a rounding one.

No contract violated. driveCurrent is a `std::upper_bound` over an already-owned `std::vector` — no heap allocation (PC-1), no per-cell virtual dispatch (PC-2), no std::function (PC-5), no exception/lock/IO (PC-4). It is a single definition called from multiple sites, so calling it again is the opposite of a PC-10 duplication. The suggested resolveControl helper is likewise safe provided it stays a concrete non-virtual function taking the segment by const ref.
verdict.revised_proposal:
Keep the finding, but fix the proposal — the one-line patch as written is INCOMPLETE and would introduce a second, worse defect.

`after_current` is initialised once at line 585 and is NOT reset to `current` before the bisection-accept ladder at 686-701. If the drive_cycle arm is added only at 586-604, then on an event step the accepted length is `high` (684) while `after_current` still holds `driveCurrent(*cycle, local_time + dt)` — a current sampled BEYOND the accepted end time, pushed at 721-724 against `time + high`. The lag would be replaced by an overshoot.

The drive_cycle arm must be added to all three ladders, each with its own sub-step length:
  - 586-604:  `else if (status == Success && segment.mode == ControlMode::drive_cycle) after_current = driveCurrent(*cycle, local_time + dt);`
  - 636-654:  `... middle_current = driveCurrent(*cycle, local_time + middle);`
  - 686-701:  `... after_current = driveCurrent(*cycle, local_time + high);`
(`cycle` is non-null in every drive_cycle path — guaranteed by 345-347 and 420-423.)

Register the band BEFORE running: with the fix, core_Experiment_test.cpp:581 becomes `CHECK(solution.current.back() == Catch::Approx(0.0));` (driveCurrent at local_time 1.0 returns `cycle.current.back()` via the `local_time >= cycle.time.back()` early-out at 314-315), and `solution.current[9]` becomes -0.25, not 1.0 — that assertion must be re-registered too, not just the last one. All three 9C-3 hash triples (Debug / Release / Release+IPO) at core_Experiment_test.cpp:~320-333 need re-recording for BOTH the current and voltage components; the appended `batch.state().raw()` component must be UNCHANGED for that fixture, and that invariance is the arbiter proving the patch is reporting-only there — if the state hash moves, the patch has leaked into the applied current and is wrong.

Whichever arm is chosen, the omission stops being silent. If instead the current behaviour is kept, the comment at 459 must say the left-endpoint value is deliberate BECAUSE it is the current `advance()` actually holds constant over the interval, and Experiment.hpp:28 must document that a drive_cycle sample reports the current applied over the PRECEDING interval while every other mode reports the value at the sample instant — and the same note must warn that `current_cutoff`/`custom_terminations` on a drive_cycle segment therefore fire against the preceding interval's current.

Add the missing coverage either way: no test in tests/ exercises a drive_cycle segment carrying a current_cutoff or a current-reading custom termination (grep of tests/ for registerDriveCycle/drive_cycle returns only parse tests, the P5-G1 run at 541-581, the 9C-3 hash test at ~250-333, allocation tests in core_ParserAllocation_test.cpp, and the missing-cycle rejection at 941-942). That gap is why (2) above went unnoticed.

Rolling the three ladders into one exhaustive `switch` over ControlMode (the dup-control-resolve helper) is the right structural close, since it makes the drive_cycle and custom_differential cases impossible to omit again — but land the behavioural decision first, under its own registered hashes, so the refactor can then be gated as digit-identical.

title: Simulation::solve has two different failure contracts and neither the asymmetry nor the mid-run one is tested
proposal:
Two gaps, both cheap and both invariant-based rather than fixture replay.

Test 1 — "Simulation::solve reports a truncated prefix and a consistent batch after a mid-run step failure". Build with make_simulation_input at 2 lanes, `{ .current_A = 1e12, .duration = 3.0, .step = 1.0 }` (the same extreme current that core_Simulation_test.cpp:174-176 already uses to force EulerLegacy into Invalid_states). Assert: the returned Status equals `solution.termination` and is not Success; `solution.time.size() == solution.terminal_voltage.size() / lanes` — the structural invariant the resize pair is there to maintain, and which nothing checks today; `solution.time.size() == completed + 1` where completed is recovered from `batch().state().at(layout.elapsed_time, 0, 0) / step`; and `std::ranges::is_sorted(solution.time)`. This also documents, by assertion, that solve is *not* atomic in the batch, which currently only the code says.

Test 2 — "a partial final step conserves total elapsed time exactly". The sum invariant is the natural analytic oracle and is stronger than the fixed `{0,1,2,2.5}` list at core_Simulation_test.cpp:212: for any (duration, step) accepted by solve, `solution.time.back() - solution.time.front() == experiment.duration` bit-for-bit, and `batch().state().at(layout.elapsed_time,0,0)` equals the same. Run it over the boundary cases the snap logic at Simulation.cpp:39-51 exists to handle — duration = 3.0 with step 1.0, duration = std::nextafter(3.0, 4.0), duration = 0.3 with step 0.1, and duration < step — as a single loop. Note that Simulation.cpp:81-83 reconstructs the final dt as `duration - completed*step` rather than accumulating, so this invariant should hold exactly; if it does not for some pair, the test has found the roundoff path the snap tolerance was written to close. Both tests are sub-millisecond and use the existing make_simulation_input, so they satisfy MC-4 and the short-gate rule.

verdict.reason:
PARTIALLY REAL — the core gap is confirmed, the framing and half the proposal are refuted.

CONFIRMED. Both quoted snippets exist verbatim. Simulation.cpp:34-37 is the pre-flight return, and Simulation.cpp:85-91 reads exactly as quoted: `solution.termination = status; solution.time.resize(completed + 1); solution.terminal_voltage.resize((completed + 1) * lanes); output = std::move(solution); return status;`. The test at core_Simulation_test.cpp:220-225 is quoted correctly. Grep over all of tests/ for `.solve(` and `current_A` confirms the reviewer's decisive claim: EVERY Simulation::solve call site in the repo passes `.current_A = 0.0` — core_Simulation_test.cpp:206,222,230,240,253,269,287,294,301 and core_P1G2_allocation_test.cpp:219 (`{ .current_A = 0.0, .duration = 16.0, .step = 1.0 }`). Nothing reaches line 85. The structural invariant `time.size() == terminal_voltage.size()/lanes` that the resize pair maintains is asserted nowhere.

REFUTED #1 — "two contracts" is wrong; there are THREE. Simulation.cpp:76-77 (`if (status != slide::Status::Success) return status;` after the pre-loop `batch_.terminalVoltage`) returns AFTER `solution` exists but WITHOUT assigning `output` and WITHOUT setting `solution.termination`. The reviewer missed it, and Test 1 is exposed to it: if the extreme current makes the pre-loop observation fail, solve returns at 77, `output` is never written, and every Test 1 assertion fails. [inferred] it will not fail — the only Invalid_states guard on that path is SpmObservables.hpp:467, `if (!(primal_value(z_surface) > 0.0 && primal_value(z_surface) < 1.0)) return slide::Status::Invalid_states;`, which keys on surface stoichiometry (in range at the initial state, x_0 = 0.2/0.8), not on current. Not run; the test must be written to tolerate it.

REFUTED #2 — the "asymmetry" half is already tested. Beyond 220-225 there is a whole dedicated TEST_CASE, "Simulation rejects unrepresentable solution extents atomically" (core_Simulation_test.cpp:279-307), asserting `unchanged.time == std::vector<double>{ 42.0 }` three more times. Only the mid-run branch is untested.

REFUTED #3 — Test 2 is substantially ALREADY DONE. core_Simulation_test.cpp:262-276 already loops over `std::nextafter(3.0, 0.0)` and `std::nextafter(3.0, 4.0)` at step 1.0 asserting `rounded_solution.time.back() == rounded_duration` — bit-for-bit `==`, the proposal's own invariant (time.front() is 0.0 on a fresh build). Line 240-246 covers duration < step exactly (`short_solution.time.back() == 1e-16`); 252-260 covers DBL_MIN/DBL_MAX exactly; 216-217 already cross-checks `batch().state().at(layout.elapsed_time, 0, 0) == 2.5`. The only new content is tightening line 234's `<= 1e-15` to `==` for 0.3/0.1 — a one-line edit, not a test case.

title: exactModalKernel recomputes an identical loop-invariant Arrhenius factor three times and open-codes molar_flux_sign twice

verdict.reason:

(1) The quoted code exists verbatim. `CudaSpmRuntime.cu:74-76` is `for (int domain = 0; domain < 2; ++domain) {` / `const double arrhenius = spm_scalar::arrheniusFactor(params.reference_temperature, temperature, params.Rg);`. Line 104-105 is the byte-identical expression at kernel scope. Lines 86 and 141 are both exactly `const double sign = domain == 0 ? 1.0 : -1.0;`. Lines 151-152 are `constexpr int neg = 0;` / `constexpr int pos = 1;`. `CellDesign.hpp:36-39` is `constexpr int molar_flux_sign(Domain domain) { return domain == Domain::neg ? 1 : -1; }`.

(2) Loop-invariance is genuine, not assumed. All three arguments are read outside the loop: `temperature` at :71 (`const double temperature = get(state, params.stride, params.temperature_row, lane);`), and `params.reference_temperature` / `params.Rg` are plain scalars in `KernelParams` (CudaSpmData.hpp:57,60), not the `[2]`-indexed fields. One thread = one lane, so unlike the CPU path (SpmObservables.hpp:285, where `T[c]` varies per lane inside the loop and recomputation is required) the CUDA value is a true kernel-scope constant.

(3) The "duplicate" is not numerically distinct, and one helper covers both sign sites with no flags. `CudaSpmBatch.cpp:90-94` builds the kernel arrays as `const auto d = domain_index(domain); params.z_row[d] = ...`, so kernel `domain` 0/1 IS `domain_index(Domain::neg/pos)` — the correspondence is by construction, not coincidence. And the CPU uses the same helper for BOTH of the kernel's uses: `SpmObservables.hpp:174` `spm_scalar::molarFlux(static_cast<Real>(molar_flux_sign(domain)), ...)` matches CudaSpmRuntime.cu:87-88, and `SpmObservables.hpp:481` `spm_scalar::activationArgument(static_cast<Real>(molar_flux_sign(domain)), ctx.i_app[lane], area, thickness, exchange_current)` matches CudaSpmRuntime.cu:142-143. The CUDA kernel is indeed the sole open-coded copy.

(4) Digit-identical, provably, not just plausibly. `arrheniusFactor` (SpmScalarKernels.hpp:111-119) is `(Scalar{1.0}/reference_temperature - Scalar{1.0}/temperature)/gas_constant` — pure, and division-only. FMA contraction (nvcc's `-fmad=true`) fuses mul+add pairs; there is no contractible mul+add anywhere in the producing expression, and its sole consumer `activatedValue` (SpmScalarKernels.hpp:122-128) is `reference * exponential(activation * arrhenius)` — a bare multiply feeding `exp`, again with no add to fuse. So collapsing three evaluations to one cannot change any rounding. The sign replacement substitutes the identical literals 1.0/-1.0; `neg`/`pos` are pure array indices (`surface_stoichiometry[pos]`, `params.specific_area_row[neg]`), so `domain_index` returning `std::size_t` is harmless. There is also no early return between :71 and :104 (first return is :122), so hoisting never adds work to a previously-skipped path.

(5) No contract violation, and I checked the gates that actually parse this file. `tests/structural/pc10_single_source.cmake:74` loads `src/core/CudaSpmRuntime.cu` and at :132-147 only does `require_tokens(...)` — presence, not counts — for `"spm_scalar::arrheniusFactor("`. Collapsing three occurrences to one still leaves the token present, so the PC-10 gate still passes. The `forbid_tokens("CUDA" ... "expm1(" "sqrt(" "asinh(" "1.0/6.0" "/24.0")` list at :148-149 is untouched. On layering, `p9c5_public_surface.cmake:5-6` states the rule as "no api/support header may include an internal one"; the loop at :153-158 skips `if(tier STREQUAL "internal")` and only walks headers with a pinned classification. A `.cu` translation unit including the `@surface api` `CellDesign.hpp` is the permitted direction and is not scanned at all. `src/core/CMakeLists.txt:11` gives the target `target_include_directories(slide_cuda_runtime PRIVATE ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src)`, so the include resolves. If anything the change moves toward PC-10 ("ONE physics source"), it does not strain it.

Where the reviewer is wrong, on two points that do not sink the finding:
- The citation `SpmObservables.hpp:200` is incorrect — line 200 is `}` closing `computeSpmTransport`'s lane loop. The real call sites are 144, 156, 174, 282, 481.
- The fallback proposal is self-contradictory. `static_assert(lane_flux_sign[0] == molar_flux_sign(Domain::neg) && ...)` names `molar_flux_sign` and `Domain`, both of which live in `CellDesign.hpp` — so the "cheap alternative that keeps the dependency-light boundary intact" requires the very include it claims to avoid. The boundary framing is also misplaced: the include would land in `CudaSpmRuntime.cu`, not in `CudaSpmData.hpp` (`@surface internal`, CudaSpmData.hpp:4), which the proposal does not touch at all.

Finally, on value: nvcc will almost certainly already CSE the three identical pure evaluations, so there is no performance claim here. This is a readability/duplication cleanup only, which is how it is filed ([duplication]) — the parent should not sell it as a speedup.

title: solveOne evaluates the full observable twice per sample: step() computes and discards exactly the observation the caller then recomputes

verdict.reason:
The redundancy is REAL and verified. ForwardSensitivity.cpp:192 ends step() with `const Dual voltage = observe();` used only for `is_finite(voltage.value) && is_finite(voltage.derivative)`, and :311-315 does `const auto status = model.step(dt); ... observation = model.observe();`. I checked the one thing that would have refuted purity: IndexedPiecewiseLinear could have carried a mutable cached search index, but `grep -n "mutable"` over CompiledCurve.hpp, SpmScalarKernels.hpp and Dual.hpp returns nothing, and the bin->segment table is built once in build() into segment_ (CompiledCurve.hpp:112-122); `Real eval(const Real &x) const` (:132) is stateless. DualSpm is in an anonymous namespace and grep for `.step(`/`observe()` across src and tests returns ONLY lines 79, 192, 298, 311, 315 of this file, so solveOne is provably the sole caller; between the two calls only `simulation_time` (a local, never address-taken) is written. So the second evaluation is genuinely redundant.

BUT the proposal's stated justification -- "Digit-identical: same function, same state, same call order -- the discarded value and the recomputed value are bit-equal by construction" -- is refuted by the repo's own recorded evidence. src/core/SpmScalarKernels.hpp:170-176: "Release builds intentionally permit reassociation and vectorisation.  A normal inline-call boundary changed those choices under Clang -Ofast even with always_inline, violating the recorded-bit contract.  This one hygienically-prefixed statement kernel keeps the expression tree in one source while preserving each backend's existing math entry points and loop IR." The proposal moves the surviving observe() from the solveOne call site (:315) one inline level deeper into step() (:192) -- exactly the "changed inline-call boundary" the project has already been burned by. observe() contains a reduction loop at :90-92 (`surface += spectral_.C[d][0][mode] * z_[d][mode]`), the canonical reassociation/vectorisation target, plus 2 sqrt and 2 asinh (SpmScalarKernels.hpp:72-98). The gate at core_ForwardSensitivity_test.cpp:202-207 carries three distinct hash constants (SLIDE_TEST_IPO && __FAST_MATH__, __FAST_MATH__, strict), i.e. the project already concedes these bits are build-mode dependent. Today the :192 value is discarded, so no test would notice if the two inlined instances already disagree under -Ofast; after the change the :192 instance becomes the reported one. Digit-identical holds under strict IEEE only, NOT "by construction" across the gated fast-math variants.

Perf rationale is also overstated and uncited: step() runs 2*NCH modal advances each with an exp AND an expm1 (SpmScalarKernels.hpp:189-190) = 48 transcendentals at NCH=12, versus observe()'s 2 sqrt + 2 asinh + 2 curve evals + 24 multiply-adds. observe() is plausibly the cheaper half, so "the expensive half of a sample" and "halves the observable cost of the whole sensitivity solve" are [inferred] with no benchmark named.

No contract violated (PLAN.md 1.1-1.3): PC-10 "ONE physics source" is helped not violated (removes a duplicate evaluation, adds no formula); no hot-path allocation (PC-1), no virtual dispatch (PC-2), no std::function in inner loops (PC-5), no api/support header including an internal one (MC-5).

title: Every validation and failure arm in CudaSpmBatch::step, CudaAsyncRecorder::enqueue and the BatchExecutor inline path is unexercised
proposal:
Three short gate tests, all analytic invariants, no long simulation:

1. `TEST_CASE("CUDA step rejects a malformed request without advancing device state", "[core][cuda][validation]")` — build a 2-lane batch, `gpu.downloadState()` and snapshot `gpu.hostBatch().state().raw()`. Then assert each rejection returns Invalid_parameters: wrong-size span (`density.first(1)`), a NaN entry (`std::bit_cast<double>(UINT64_C(0x7ff8000000000000))`), `dt == 0.0`, `dt < 0.0`, non-finite `time`. Then `REQUIRE(gpu.downloadState() == Status::Success)` and `CHECK(std::memcmp(snapshot.data(), gpu.hostBatch().state().raw().data(), bytes) == 0)`. The memcmp is the load-bearing assertion: a rejected step must be a no-op on the arena, which is exactly the property the half-advanced-state early return at CudaSpmRuntime.cu:125 makes non-obvious.

2. `TEST_CASE("CUDA recorder thins by cadence and rejects a non-increasing accepted step", "[core][cuda][recorder][validation]")` — configure with `{ .cadence = 3, .ring_slots = 3 }`, enqueue steps 1..6, assert `snapshotsWritten() == 2` (only 3 and 6 satisfy `step % 3 == 0`) and that a subsequent `enqueue(6)` returns Invalid_parameters while `enqueue(9)` returns Success. Exact counts, no tolerance.

3. `TEST_CASE("single-worker BatchExecutor reports a throwing callback and still visits every index", "[core][thread-pool][batch-executor]")` — `executor.configure(3, 1)`, callback increments visits[index] then throws at index 1. Assert the returned Status is Unknown_problem, that all three visits equal 1 (the "all tasks finish after a failure" contract documented at ThreadPool.hpp:62-64 applies to the inline arm too), and that a throw at index 2 alongside an Invalid_parameters return at index 1 yields Invalid_parameters — pinning that the inline arm's `first` selection at ThreadPool.hpp:151-152 keeps the LOWEST-index failure, matching the pool arm gate at core_ThreadPool_test.cpp:94-111.

verdict.reason: All three quoted blocks exist verbatim at the cited lines and mean what the reviewer says. Arm 1 — CudaSpmBatch.cpp:266-271 is exactly `if (!valid() || static_cast<int>(current_density.size()) != n_lanes() || !is_finite(time) || !is_finite(dt) || !(dt > 0.0)) return slide::Status::Invalid_parameters;` plus the per-element finiteness loop. I grepped every `gpu.step(` in tests/: core_CudaSpmBatch_test.cpp:123,163,210,279,320, all correctly sized/finite/dt>0. The only other hit is core_CudaDisabled_test.cpp:27 `CHECK(batch.step(current_density, 0.0, 1.0) == Status::NotImplementedYet)`, and tests/unit/CMakeLists.txt:229-238 builds that file only in the `else()` branch of `if(SLIDE_WITH_CUDA)` — i.e. exactly when lines 266-271 are compiled out. Genuine gap. Arm 2 — CudaSpmBatch.cpp:520-524 verbatim. src/core/AsyncRecorder.hpp:39 `std::size_t cadence{ 1 };`, and the test's designated init at :304-306 sets only ring_slots/backpressure/codec, so `accepted_step % 1 != 0` is never true; :321 enqueues `step + 1` for step 0..5, strictly increasing, so `accepted_step <= previous_step` never fires. core_AsyncRecorder_test.cpp:404-407 does gate monotonicity, but on the host `AsyncRecorder` (two-arg `enqueue(step, current)`) — a different class from `CudaAsyncRecorder` (one-arg), so not a duplicate. Arm 3 — ThreadPool.hpp:144-153 verbatim. ThreadPool.cpp:75-98: `workers = min(workers, batches)` then `if (workers > 1) pool = pool_factory_(workers)`, so `configure(3,1)` → workers=1 → pool_ == nullptr → inline arm. The existing inline test (core_ThreadPool_test.cpp:212-219) uses `configure(1, 7)` with a non-throwing callback returning Success; :204 `parallelFor(4,...)` short-circuits at `count > batches_`; :207 runs under `configure(3,7)` → workers=3 → pool arm. So the inline catch and the `first` selection at 151-152 are both unexercised. The pool-side catch the reviewer points at is indeed separate code (ThreadPool.cpp:149-154). TWO EVIDENCE ERRORS the reviewer got wrong, neither fatal: (a) "`CHECK(recorder.thinnedSnapshots() == 0)` at :330 is consistent with cadence-thinning never being attempted" is a misread — CudaSpmBatch.cpp:586-591 returns `impl_->thinned + impl_->writer.thinnedSnapshots()`, and `impl_->thinned` is incremented ONLY in the backpressure branch at :536; a cadence skip at :521 returns Success touching no counter, so that CHECK is silent about cadence. The actual evidence is the `cadence{1}` default. (b) "the half-advanced-state early return at CudaSpmRuntime.cu:125" — the `nan("")` is at .cu:123 and the `return;` at 124, and it lives inside the device kernel, which is never reached when host validation rejects at :266-271 (the function returns before `launchStep`). So proposal 1's memcmp is trivially true, not load-bearing for the stated reason. Contracts: PLAN.md §1.1 PC-1/PC-4 bind the accepted-step hot path, not test code; PC-10 ("every formula exists in exactly one scalar-generic definition") is untouched — no physics is duplicated; §1.3 MC-2/MC-4 ("Tests mirror source names") are satisfied because all three cases land in the existing mirror-named files. Tests-only, no arithmetic, so digit-identical trivially.
verdict.revised_proposal: Keep all three cases; fix proposal 2, which as written would pass for the wrong reason and leave the target arm still unexercised. `snapshotsWritten()` (CudaSpmBatch.cpp:594-596) reads the async writer's counter and is only deterministic after `finish()` — that is why the existing test calls finish() at :328 before checking at :329. But `finish()` sets `impl_->finished = true` (:582), and enqueue's FIRST guard at :518 is `if (impl_ == nullptr || impl_->finished) return Invalid_parameters`. A post-finish `enqueue(6)` therefore returns Invalid_parameters via the finished guard and never reaches the monotonicity check at :523-524. Correct order: configure `{ .cadence = 3, .ring_slots = 3, .backpressure = block }`; enqueue 1..6 (each preceded by gpu.step so a snapshot exists); then CHECK(enqueue(6) == Invalid_parameters) — monotonicity, since previous_step was set only at 3 and 6; then CHECK(enqueue(9) == Success); THEN finish(); then CHECK(snapshotsWritten() == 3), not 2 — steps 3, 6 and 9 all satisfy `% 3 == 0`. Optionally CHECK(thinnedSnapshots() == 0) to pin that cadence skips are NOT counted as thinning. Proposal 1: keep, but drop the CudaSpmRuntime.cu rationale — the memcmp is a cheap no-op check, not a probe of the kernel's early return, because validation returns before launchStep. Two mechanical fixes: `density.first(1)` does not compile on a std::array — use `std::span<const double>{ density }.first(1)`; and prefer `std::numeric_limits<double>::quiet_NaN()` (add `<limits>`) over the bit_cast, since the file does not include `<bit>`. Also add an infinite-dt case, since `!(dt > 0.0)` alone does not catch `+inf`, which is caught by `!is_finite(dt)` — a separate sub-arm. Proposal 3: keep as written; `configure(3, 1)` provably selects the inline arm via ThreadPool.cpp:84-89, and the two asserted behaviours follow from ThreadPool.hpp:144-153 (the try/catch means indices 0,1,2 are all visited after a throw at 1; `first` is only overwritten while it is still Success, so an Invalid_parameters at index 1 survives a throw at index 2). Note in the test title or a comment that these three cases are CUDA-build-gated (proposals 1 and 2 land in a file compiled only under SLIDE_WITH_CUDA=ON per tests/unit/CMakeLists.txt:229-231), so they add no coverage to the default build.
